# Yash Chopra(1932-2012)

*   Producer
*   Director
*   Additional Crew

[IMDbPro Starmeter](https://pro.imdb.com/name/nm0007181/?rf=cons_nm_meter&ref_=cons_nm_meter)[See rank](https://pro.imdb.com/name/nm0007181/?rf=cons_nm_meter&ref_=cons_nm_meter)

![Image 3: Yash Chopra](https://m.media-amazon.com/images/M/MV5BMTg3NDYwODk4NF5BMl5BanBnXkFtZTcwNzEzNDg3OA@@._V1_QL75_UY207_CR4,0,140,207_.jpg)

[](https://www.imdb.com/name/nm0007181/mediaviewer/rm1974578176/?ref_=nm_ov_ph)

[](https://www.imdb.com/name/nm0007181/bio/?ref_=nm_ov_bio_sm)

Labeled the eternal romantic and with one of the best musical senses in the business, [Yash Chopra](https://www.imdb.com/name/nm0007181/?ref_=nm_ov_bio_lk) is arguably India's most successful director of romantic films. Although he made action-oriented films like the ever-popular [Deewaar (1975)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt0072860/?ref_=nm_ov_bio_lk), it is in tackling love and its various aspects that he has been at his best. One of the few remaining commercial Indian directors who started their careers in the 1950s, he has successfully moved with the times from the socially significant [Dhool Ka Phool (1959)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt0052736/?ref_=nm_ov_bio_lk) to the young and cool [Dil To Pagal Hai (1997)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt0118983/?ref_=nm_ov_bio_lk).  
  
Yash Chopra was born in Lahore in 1932, to an accountant in the PWD division of the British Punjab administration, the youngest of eight children. He began as an assistant director to [I.S. Johar](https://www.imdb.com/name/nm0424102/?ref_=nm_ov_bio_lk) before working with his elder brother, the legendary [B.R. Chopra](https://www.imdb.com/name/nm0159148/?ref_=nm_ov_bio_lk); while another brother, [Dharam Chopra](https://www.imdb.com/name/nm0159150/?ref_=nm_ov_bio_lk), worked as his cameraman. He was given his first directorial opportunity with [Dhool Ka Phool (1959)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt0052736/?ref_=nm_ov_bio_lk), a melodrama about illegitimacy; it became a hit and even now remains popular today. Encouraged by this success, the Chopra brothers made a few more movies together, the most notable being [Waqt (1965)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt0059893/?ref_=nm_ov_bio_lk), India's first multi-starrer; and [Ittefaq (1969)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt0064506/?ref_=nm_ov_bio_lk), a thriller. On the personal front, Chopra married [Pamela Chopra](https://www.imdb.com/name/nm0159158/?ref_=nm_ov_bio_lk) (née Singh) in 1970, and they had two children, [Aditya Chopra](https://www.imdb.com/name/nm0159147/?ref_=nm_ov_bio_lk) and [Uday Chopra](https://www.imdb.com/name/nm0159167/?ref_=nm_ov_bio_lk), both working in the film industry today.  
  
In 1973, the Chopra brothers separated, with Yash Chopra founded his studio, Yash Raj Films, and launched it with [Daag: A Poem of Love (1973)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt0150251/?ref_=nm_ov_bio_lk), a successful melodrama about a polygamous man. He then entered one of his best phases with two [Amitabh Bachchan](https://www.imdb.com/name/nm0000821/?ref_=nm_ov_bio_lk) classics: [Deewaar (1975)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt0072860/?ref_=nm_ov_bio_lk) and [Kabhi Kabhie (1976)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt0074730/?ref_=nm_ov_bio_lk). These movies set the standard for the 1970s and 1980s, establishing Bachchan as the greatest and most beloved Indian film star of all time. His respective roles--a bitter criminal and a sensitive, brooding poet--are considered to be his greatest performances, although complete opposites of each other.  
  
In the 1980s, Chopra went through a rough time. Two of his melodramas, [Silsila (1981)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt0083081/?ref_=nm_ov_bio_lk) and [Faasle (1985)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt0089119/?ref_=nm_ov_bio_lk); and two action-oriented films, [Mashaal (1984)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt0085912/?ref_=nm_ov_bio_lk) and [Vijay (1988)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt0096390/?ref_=nm_ov_bio_lk), flopped at the box office, although the latter became a critically acclaimed classic years later. However, he made a comeback with his musical love triangle [Chandni (1989)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt0097045/?ref_=nm_ov_bio_lk). The film was a huge success, with great performances by established heroine [Sridevi](https://www.imdb.com/name/nm0004437/?ref_=nm_ov_bio_lk) and action hero [Vinod Khanna](https://www.imdb.com/name/nm0451396/?ref_=nm_ov_bio_lk). Then came what critics and Chopra himself considered his best film, [Lamhe (1991)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt0102258/?ref_=nm_ov_bio_lk), a beautiful film about cross-generational love. It couldn't survive the box office, however, due to its incestuous nature.  
  
[Parampara (1993)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt0107777/?ref_=nm_ov_bio_lk), done for an outside producer, was a misfire, but then came the box-office hit and trend setter [Darr (1993)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt0109555/?ref_=nm_ov_bio_lk). Starring the then-débutant [Shah Rukh Khan](https://www.imdb.com/name/nm0451321/?ref_=nm_ov_bio_lk), it showed a sympathetic look at obsessive love and an emotion often overlooked in love--fear--and its success catapulted Khan to super-stardom. In 1995, Chopra turned to production and [Aditya Chopra](https://www.imdb.com/name/nm0159147/?ref_=nm_ov_bio_lk) made his directorial debut with [Dilwale Dulhania Le Jayenge (1995)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt0112870/?ref_=nm_ov_bio_lk), which had the longest-running initial release in cinema history. He directed one more film, [Dil To Pagal Hai (1997)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt0118983/?ref_=nm_ov_bio_lk), a love story set against the theater, which became a huge success and a cult hit, before he retired from directing. However, in 2004, he made a grand comeback with [Veer Zaara (2004)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt0420332/?ref_=nm_ov_bio_lk), a touching cross-border love story, which he said would be his last directorial effort.

**Syed Jaaved Ahmed Jaffrey** (Hindustani pronunciation:[[d͡ʒɑːʋɛd̪d͡ʒɑːfɾiː]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Help:IPA/Hindi_and_Urdu "Help:IPA/Hindi and Urdu"); born 4 December 1962) is an Indian actor, dancer,[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Javed_Jaffrey#cite_note-Javed_Jaffrey:_Dance_shows_are_more_focussed_on_the_reality_part-2)[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Javed_Jaffrey#cite_note-Javed_Jaffrey_to_turn_director-3) producer and comedian who has appeared in [Hindi](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hindi "Hindi") films and television shows. He is the son of the comedian [Jagdeep](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jagdeep "Jagdeep"). He joined the [Aam Aadmi Party](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Aam_Aadmi_Party "Aam Aadmi Party") (AAP) in March 2014 and contested the [2014 Indian general election](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2014_Indian_general_election "2014 Indian general election") from the [Lucknow](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lucknow_Lok_Sabha_constituency "Lucknow Lok Sabha constituency") constituency finishing fifth.[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Javed_Jaffrey#cite_note-4)

Jaffrey has been awarded the life membership of International Film And Television Club of Asian Academy of Film & Television.[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Javed_Jaffrey#cite_note-5) He was also the brand ambassador of the first India International Animation and Cartoon Film festival 2015.[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Javed_Jaffrey#cite_note-6)[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Javed_Jaffrey#cite_note-7)

## Early life and education

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Jaaved_Jaaferi&action=edit&section=1 "Edit section: Early life and education")]

Jaffrey is the son of comedian [Jagdeep](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jagdeep "Jagdeep").[[8]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Javed_Jaffrey#cite_note-8) He was born in Bombay, [Maharashtra](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Maharashtra "Maharashtra"), India (present-day [Mumbai](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mumbai "Mumbai")).

He participated in school dance competitions at [St. Theresa's](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/St._Teresa's_High_School,_Charni_Road "St. Teresa's High School, Charni Road"), and later while studying [psychology](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Psychology "Psychology") at National College (his parents discouraged him from attending [St. Xavier's](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/St._Xavier's_College,_Mumbai "St. Xavier's College, Mumbai"), fearing it would make him "go wild"). In 1983, he won an all-India dance competition that awarded him training at a [London](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/London "London") dance school, which cemented his career in dance.[[9]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Javed_Jaffrey#cite_note-Johny_come_lately-9)

He married Habiba Jaffrey in 1991 and has a daughter and two sons, including actor [Meezaan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Meezaan_Jafri "Meezaan Jafri").

## Media career

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Jaaved_Jaaferi&action=edit&section=2 "Edit section: Media career")]

### Films

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Jaaved_Jaaferi&action=edit&section=3 "Edit section: Films")]

The film _[Meri Jung](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Meri\_Jung "Meri Jung")_, released in 1985, gave him his first opportunity to enact the role of a villain and showcase his dancing powers on screen.[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Javed_Jaffrey#cite_note-Javed_Jaffrey:_Dance_shows_are_more_focussed_on_the_reality_part-2)[[10]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Javed_Jaffrey#cite_note-'The_Forest'_shows_what_we_are_inside:_Javed_Jaffrey-10)

He won his first [IIFA Award](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/International_Indian_Film_Academy_Awards "International Indian Film Academy Awards") for best comic role in _[Salaam Namaste](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Salaam\_Namaste "Salaam Namaste")_ in 2005.

In 2008, he played Charlie Anna in the animated film _[Roadside Romeo](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Roadside\_Romeo "Roadside Romeo")_, a collaborative effort of [Yash Raj Films](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Yash_Raj_Films "Yash Raj Films") and [Disney](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Disney "Disney").

He has produced or co-produced films and documentaries such as _[Inshallah, Football](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Inshallah,\_Football "Inshallah, Football")_ and _[Inshallah, Kashmir](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Inshallah,\_Kashmir "Inshallah, Kashmir")._[[11]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Javed_Jaffrey#cite_note-Devarsi_Ghosh-11)

### Television

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Jaaved_Jaaferi&action=edit&section=4 "Edit section: Television")]

The launch of [cable TV](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cable_television "Cable television") in the 1990s, particularly [Channel [V]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Channel_V_India "Channel V India") and its irreverent sense of humour, gave him a niche to depict his brand of comedy.[[12]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Javed_Jaffrey#cite_note-12) He has been called "TVdom's first real superstar".[[13]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Javed_Jaffrey#cite_note-13)

He has also appeared in the [Pakistani](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pakistan "Pakistan") programme _[Loose Talk](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Loose\_Talk\_(Pakistani\_TV\_series) "Loose Talk (Pakistani TV series)")_ in the early 2000s, portraying various characters from India.

#### Advertising industry

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Jaaved_Jaaferi&action=edit&section=5 "Edit section: Advertising industry")]

He has been associated with advertising since the 1980s as an actor, [copywriter](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Copywriting "Copywriting") and producer.[[11]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Javed_Jaffrey#cite_note-Devarsi_Ghosh-11) He has appeared in the comical Maggi Hot & Sweet Sauce commercials for 25 years.[[14]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Javed_Jaffrey#cite_note-14)

#### Host and judge

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Jaaved_Jaaferi&action=edit&section=6 "Edit section: Host and judge")]

He has commentated on the Japanese TV show _[Takeshi's Castle](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Takeshi's\_Castle "Takeshi's Castle")_ and _[Ninja Warrior](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ninja\_Warrior "Ninja Warrior")_ on [Pogo TV](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pogo_(TV_channel) "Pogo (TV channel)") and [Hungama](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hungama_TV "Hungama TV") respectively. He was also the judge for Karaoke World Championships India with [Manasi Scott](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Manasi_Scott "Manasi Scott"), music director Raju Singh, [Salim Merchant](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Salim_Merchant "Salim Merchant"), [Sulaiman Merchant](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sulaiman_Merchant "Sulaiman Merchant"), founder and organizer of KWC INDIA, Savio Paul D'sa, [Leslie Lewis](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lesle_Lewis_(composer) "Lesle Lewis (composer)"), [Remo Fernandes](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Remo_Fernandes "Remo Fernandes"), and [Sunita Rao](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sunita_Rao "Sunita Rao").[[15]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Javed_Jaffrey#cite_note-15)[[16]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Javed_Jaffrey#cite_note-16)[[17]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Javed_Jaffrey#cite_note-17)

Jaffrey has hosted award shows including [Filmfare](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Filmfare_Awards "Filmfare Awards"),[[18]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Javed_Jaffrey#cite_note-18) Zee Cine Awards,[[19]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Javed_Jaffrey#cite_note-19) and [IIFA](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/IIFA_Awards "IIFA Awards").[[20]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Javed_Jaffrey#cite_note-20)[[21]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Javed_Jaffrey#cite_note-21)

Jaffrey hosted Big Googly on [BIG 92.7FM](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/BIG_FM_92.7 "BIG FM 92.7") created with [Paritosh Painter](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Paritosh_Painter "Paritosh Painter"). He also hosted Once More, where he talks about Bollywood films from the 1970s to the 1990s in his comic style, on Epic channel since 2015.[[22]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Javed_Jaffrey#cite_note-22)[[23]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Javed_Jaffrey#cite_note-23)

He anchored the show _Flashback_.[[9]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Javed_Jaffrey#cite_note-Johny_come_lately-9) Jaffrey also anchored the song programme, _Timex Timepass_, in which he shifted between the caricatures of characters.[_[citation needed](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wikipedia:Citation\_needed "Wikipedia:Citation needed")_][[24]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Javed_Jaffrey#cite_note-24)

From 1996 to 2014 he hosted the dance competition show _[Boogie Woogie](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Boogie\_Woogie\_(Indian\_TV\_series) "Boogie Woogie (Indian TV series)")_ on Sony Entertainment Television Asia with his brother Naved Jaffery and friend [Ravi Behl](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ravi_Behl "Ravi Behl").[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Javed_Jaffrey#cite_note-Javed_Jaffrey:_Dance_shows_are_more_focussed_on_the_reality_part-2)[[25]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Javed_Jaffrey#cite_note-TV_offers_opportunities_to_every_talent:_Javed_Jaffrey-25)

## Political career

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Jaaved_Jaaferi&action=edit&section=7 "Edit section: Political career")]

Jaffrey contested the 2014 Lok Sabha Elections from [Lucknow](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lucknow_(Lok_Sabha_constituency) "Lucknow (Lok Sabha constituency)") as a candidate of [Aam Aadmi Party](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Aam_Aadmi_Party "Aam Aadmi Party") but lost to BJP's [Rajnath Singh](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rajnath_Singh "Rajnath Singh"). He had finished fifth in the constituency securing 41,429 votes.[[26]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Javed_Jaffrey#cite_note-26)

**IMDb**, formerly known as the **Internet Movie Database**, is an [online database](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Online_database "Online database") of information related to films, television series, podcasts, video games, and streaming content online – including cast, production crew and biographies, plot summaries, trivia, ratings, and fan and critical reviews. As of September 2025, IMDb ranks as the 40th most visited website in the world and the 35th in the United States.[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/IMDb_(identifier)#cite_note-2)[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/IMDb_(identifier)#cite_note-3)

The database contained some 25.9 million titles, and 14.8 million person records as of September 2025.[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/IMDb_(identifier)#cite_note-stats_2022.12-4)[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/IMDb_(identifier)#cite_note-5)

## Features

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=IMDb&action=edit&section=1 "Edit section: Features")]

User profile pages show a user's registration date and, optionally, their personal ratings of titles. Since 2015, "badges" can be added showing a count of contributions. These badges range from total contributions made to independent categories such as photos, trivia, and biographies. If a registered user or visitor is in the entertainment industry and has an IMDb page, they can add photos through IMDbPRO.[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/IMDb_(identifier)#cite_note-6)

### User ratings of films

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=IMDb&action=edit&section=2 "Edit section: User ratings of films")]

#### Rankings

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=IMDb&action=edit&section=3 "Edit section: Rankings")]

The IMDb Top 250 is a [list](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List "List") of the top-rated 250 films, based on ratings by registered users of the website using the methods described. As of June 23,2026[[update]](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=IMDb&action=edit), _[The Shawshank Redemption](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_Shawshank\_Redemption "The Shawshank Redemption")_ (1994), directed by [Frank Darabont](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Frank_Darabont "Frank Darabont"), is the highest-ranked film on the list, and has been since 2008.[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/IMDb_(identifier)#cite_note-AVFilm14-7)[[8]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/IMDb_(identifier)#cite_note-vanityfair-8)[[9]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/IMDb_(identifier)#cite_note-9) The "Top 250" rating is based on only the ratings of "regular voters". The number of votes a registered user would have to make to be considered as a user who votes regularly has been kept secret. IMDb has stated that to maintain the effectiveness of the Top 250 list they "_deliberately do not disclose the criteria used for a person to be counted as a regular voter_".[[10]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/IMDb_(identifier)#cite_note-10) In addition to other weightings, the Top 250 films are also based on a weighted rating formula referred to in [actuarial science](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Actuarial_science "Actuarial science") as a _credibility formula_.[[11]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/IMDb_(identifier)#cite_note-11) This label arises because a statistic is taken to be more credible the greater the number of individual pieces of information; in this case from eligible users who submit ratings. Although the current formula is not disclosed, IMDb originally used the following formula to calculate their weighted rating:[[12]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/IMDb_(identifier)#cite_note-12)

The IMDb also has a Bottom 100 feature which is assembled through a similar process although only 10,000 votes must be received to qualify for the list.[[13]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/IMDb_(identifier)#cite_note-13)

The Top 250 list comprises a wide range of feature films, including major releases, cult films, independent films, critically acclaimed films, silent films, and non-English-language films. Documentaries, short films and TV episodes are not currently included.

Since 2015, there has been a Top 250 list devoted to ranking television shows.[[14]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/IMDb_(identifier)#cite_note-14)

### Reference view

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=IMDb&action=edit&section=4 "Edit section: Reference view")]

IMDb originally used a more sidebar/list-based view on title pages. However, in 2010 the site updated pages to more free-flowing layouts, and offered logged-in users an "advanced view" site preference setting called "Combined view", or this could be done on an ad-hoc basis by simply adding `/combined` to the end of the [URL](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/URL "URL") (e.g. https://www.imdb.com/title/tt2358891/combined), for users to choose should they prefer the older page view display method or to aid the editing of data.

In 2017, some alterations were made to this advanced view, and the setting was renamed "Reference view", again also able to be accessed ad-hoc by simply adding `/reference` to the end of the URL (e.g. https://www.imdb.com/title/tt2358891/reference), with the former `/combined` URLs made to link to the newer `/reference` ones.[[15]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/IMDb_(identifier)#cite_note-imdb_ref_view_1-15)

### Message boards

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=IMDb&action=edit&section=5 "Edit section: Message boards")]

By February 20, 2017, all the message boards and their content were permanently removed. According to the website, the decision was made because the boards were "no longer providing a positive, useful experience for the vast majority of our more than 250 million monthly users worldwide".[[16]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/IMDb_(identifier)#cite_note-16) Others have mentioned its susceptibility to [trolling](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Troll_(slang) "Troll (slang)") and disagreeable behavior.[[17]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/IMDb_(identifier)#cite_note-17)[[18]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/IMDb_(identifier)#cite_note-18)[[19]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/IMDb_(identifier)#cite_note-19) Needham also mentioned in a post some months earlier that the boards received less income from ads, and that their members only made up a very small part of the website's visitors. The boards were costly to run due to the system's age and dated design, which did not make business sense.[[20]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/IMDb_(identifier)#cite_note-20) The decision to remove the message boards was met with outspoken backlash from some of its users, and sparked an online petition garnering over 8,000 signatures.[[21]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/IMDb_(identifier)#cite_note-21) In the days leading up to February 20, 2017, both Archive.org[[22]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/IMDb_(identifier)#cite_note-22) and MovieChat.org[[23]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/IMDb_(identifier)#cite_note-23) preserved the entire contents of the IMDb message boards using [web scraping](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Web_scraping "Web scraping"). Archive.org and MovieChat.org have published IMDb message board archives.[[24]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/IMDb_(identifier)#cite_note-24)

### IMDbPro

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=IMDb&action=edit&section=6 "Edit section: IMDbPro")]

Actors, crew, and industry executives can post their own resume and upload photos of themselves for a yearly membership fee to IMDbPro. IMDbPro can be accessed by anyone willing to pay the annual fee of US$149.99. Membership enables a user to access the rank order of each industry personality, as well as agent contact information for any actor, producer, director etc. that has an IMDb page. IMDbPro also allows existing actors to claim their name page, as well as production companies to claim titles they own/manage. Enrolling in IMDbPro enables members who are industry personnel to upload a head shot to open their page, as well as to upload hundreds of photos to accompany their page. Anyone can register as an IMDb user and contribute to the site as well as view its content; however, those users enrolled in IMDbPro have greater access and privileges.[[25]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/IMDb_(identifier)#cite_note-25)

## History

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=IMDb&action=edit&section=7 "Edit section: History")]

IMDb began as a fan-operated movie database on the [Usenet](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Usenet "Usenet") group "rec.arts.movies" in 1990, and moved to the World Wide Web (www. system) in 1993.

### Pre-website

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=IMDb&action=edit&section=8 "Edit section: Pre-website")]

IMDb originated from a personal film database that English film enthusiast [Col Needham](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Col_Needham "Col Needham") had maintained as a hobby since 1987.[[26]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/IMDb_(identifier)#cite_note-ebsco-26) Needham, who worked as an engineer at [Hewlett-Packard](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hewlett-Packard "Hewlett-Packard") in [Bristol](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bristol "Bristol"), had been recording details of every film he watched since his teenage years.[[27]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/IMDb_(identifier)#cite_note-latimes-27)

In the late 1980s, Needham joined the [Usenet](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Usenet "Usenet") newsgroup [rec.arts.movies](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rec.arts.movies?action=edit&redlink=1 "Rec.arts.movies (page does not exist)"), where film enthusiasts exchanged information about movies. He made a posting entitled "Those Eyes" about actresses with beautiful eyes, which prompted other users to respond with additions and their own lists.[[28]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/IMDb_(identifier)#cite_note-time-28) Needham subsequently started an "Actors List", while Dave Knight began a "Directors List", and Andy Krieg took over "THE LIST" (which would later be renamed the "Actress List") from Hank Driskill.[[29]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/IMDb_(identifier)#cite_note-techcrunch-29) Both the actors and actresses lists were initially restricted to people who were alive and working, but as the project grew, retired performers were added, leading Needham to create a separate "Dead Actors/Actresses List".[[30]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/IMDb_(identifier)#cite_note-historyofdomains-30) Steve Hammond later started collecting and merging character names for both the actors and actresses lists; when these achieved popularity, they were merged back into the main lists.

By late 1990, the lists included almost 10,000 films and television series, correlated with actors and actresses appearing therein. On October 17, 1990, Needham developed and posted a collection of [Unix shell](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Unix_shell "Unix shell") scripts to the newsgroup that could be used to search the four lists, and thus the database that would become IMDb was born.[[29]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/IMDb_(identifier)#cite_note-techcrunch-29) At the time, it was known as the "rec.arts.movies movie database".

By 1992, the database had been expanded to include additional categories of filmmakers and other demographic material, as well as trivia, biographies, and plot summaries. The movie ratings had been properly integrated with the list data, and a centralized email interface for querying the database had been created by Alan Jay.[[30]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/IMDb_(identifier)#cite_note-historyofdomains-30) The database continued to be maintained by volunteer "section managers" who received contributions from users around the world.

### On the Web

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=IMDb&action=edit&section=9 "Edit section: On the Web")]

The database had been expanded to include additional categories of filmmakers and other demographic material as well as trivia, biographies, and plot summaries. The movie ratings had been properly integrated with the list data, and a centralized email interface for querying the database had been created by Alan Jay. Later, on August 5, 1993,[[31]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/IMDb_(identifier)#cite_note-31) it moved onto the fledgling [World Wide Web](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/World_Wide_Web "World Wide Web") under the name of _Cardiff Internet Movie Database_.[[32]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/IMDb_(identifier)#cite_note-32) The database resided on the servers of the computer science department of [Cardiff University](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cardiff_University "Cardiff University") in Wales. [Rob Hartill](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rob_Hartill "Rob Hartill") was the original web interface author. In 1994, the email interface was revised to accept the submission of all information, which enabled people to email the specific list maintainer with their updates. However, the structure remained so that information received on a single film was divided among multiple section managers, the sections being defined and determined by categories of film personnel and the individual filmographies contained therein. Over the next few years, the database was run on a network of [mirrors](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Web_mirror "Web mirror") across the world with donated bandwidth.[[33]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/IMDb_(identifier)#cite_note-33)

### As an independent company

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=IMDb&action=edit&section=10 "Edit section: As an independent company")]

In 1996, IMDb was incorporated in the United Kingdom, becoming the Internet Movie Database Ltd. Founder Col Needham became the primary owner. General revenue for site operations was generated through advertising, licensing and partnerships.[[34]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/IMDb_(identifier)#cite_note-imdb_inc._info_1-34)

### As Amazon.com subsidiary (1998–present)

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=IMDb&action=edit&section=11 "Edit section: As Amazon.com subsidiary (1998–present)")]

In April 1998, [Jeff Bezos](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jeff_Bezos "Jeff Bezos"), founder, owner, and [CEO](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chief_executive_officer "Chief executive officer") of Amazon.com, struck a deal with Needham and other principal shareholders to buy IMDb outright; Amazon paid $55 million for IMDb and two other companies.[[35]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/IMDb_(identifier)#cite_note-imdb_amazon_buy_1-35) Bezos attached it to Amazon as a subsidiary, private company.[[36]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/IMDb_(identifier)#cite_note-imdb_prnw_info_1-36) This gave IMDb the ability to pay the shareholders salaries for their work.[_[clarification needed](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wikipedia:Please\_clarify "Wikipedia:Please clarify")_] In the process of expanding its product line, Amazon.com intended to use IMDb as an advertising resource for selling DVDs and videotapes.

From 1996 onwards, an annual newsletter email (archived on the website) has been sent from Col Needham to contributors on the first day of each calendar year. The annual newsletter lists various information about the past year on the site, including stats, top contributors tally for the year (the top 300 users, currently; fewer in previous years), and a perspective on the site's progress and future.[[37]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/IMDb_(identifier)#cite_note-imdb_newsletter_1-37)[[38]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/IMDb_(identifier)#cite_note-imdb_newsletter_2022.01.01-38)[[39]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/IMDb_(identifier)#cite_note-imdb_newsletter_email_2022.01.01-39)

As an additional incentive for users, as of 2003[[update]](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=IMDb&action=edit), users identified as one of the "top 100 contributors" of hard data received complimentary free access to IMDbPro for the following calendar year; for 2006 this was increased to the top 150 contributors, and for 2010 to the top 250.[[40]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/IMDb_(identifier)#cite_note-imdb_top_2010-40)

In 2008, IMDb launched their first official foreign-language version with IMDb.de, in German. Also in 2008, IMDb acquired two other companies: [Withoutabox](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Withoutabox "Withoutabox")[[41]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/IMDb_(identifier)#cite_note-imdb_latimes_WAB_1-41) and [Box Office Mojo](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Box_Office_Mojo "Box Office Mojo").[[42]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/IMDb_(identifier)#cite_note-imdb_BOM_1-42)

The website was originally [Perl](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Perl "Perl")-based, but IMDb [no longer discloses what software it uses for reasons of security](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Security_through_obscurity "Security through obscurity"), apart from mentioning [The Apache Software Foundation](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Apache_Software_Foundation "The Apache Software Foundation").[[43]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/IMDb_(identifier)#cite_note-imdb_perl_1-43) In 2010, the site was [filtered in China](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Internet_censorship_in_China "Internet censorship in China").[[44]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/IMDb_(identifier)#cite_note-imdb_TR_China_info_1-44)

In 2016, _The IMDb Studio at Sundance_ was launched, a talk show that is presented on _IMDb_ and [YouTube](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/YouTube "YouTube").[[45]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/IMDb_(identifier)#cite_note-imdb_sundance_1-45)[[46]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/IMDb_(identifier)#cite_note-imdb_yt_info_1-46)

The site's message boards were disabled in February 2017. In April 2017, IMDb celebrated its 25th anniversary. As of that year, Needham was still managing IMDb from its main office in [Bristol](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bristol "Bristol") in the [Castlemead](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Castlemead "Castlemead") office tower.[[47]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/IMDb_(identifier)#cite_note-Jones-47)

In January 2019, IMDb launched an [ad-supported](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ad-supported "Ad-supported") streaming service called [Freedive](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Amazon_Freevee "Amazon Freevee").[[48]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/IMDb_(identifier)#cite_note-48) This was the company's second attempt at a streaming service; it launched a similar service in 2008.[[49]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/IMDb_(identifier)#cite_note-imdb_cnet_2008-49)[[50]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/IMDb_(identifier)#cite_note-imdb_reg_info_1-50) In June 2019, Freedive was rebranded as IMDb TV.[[51]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/IMDb_(identifier)#cite_note-imdb_amz_trippled-51) In April 2022, the service was rebranded again as Amazon Freevee.[[52]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/IMDb_(identifier)#cite_note-imdb_freevee_1-52) On December 30, 2024, it was closed as an independent site and its content was merged into [Amazon Prime Video](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Amazon_Prime_Video "Amazon Prime Video").[[53]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/IMDb_(identifier)#cite_note-53)

## Content and format

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=IMDb&action=edit&section=12 "Edit section: Content and format")]

### Data provided by subjects

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=IMDb&action=edit&section=13 "Edit section: Data provided by subjects")]

In 2006, IMDb introduced its "Résumé Subscription Service", where an actor or crew member can post their [résumé](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/R%C3%A9sum%C3%A9 "Résumé") and upload photos[[54]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/IMDb_(identifier)#cite_note-54) for a yearly fee.[[55]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/IMDb_(identifier)#cite_note-55) IMDb résumé pages are kept on a sub-page of the regular entry about that person, with a regular entry automatically created for each résumé subscriber who does not already have one.[[56]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/IMDb_(identifier)#cite_note-56)

### Copyright, vandalism and error issues

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=IMDb&action=edit&section=14 "Edit section: Copyright, vandalism and error issues")]

Volunteers who contribute content to the database technically retain copyright on their contributions, but the compilation of the content becomes the exclusive property of IMDb with the full right to copy, modify, and sublicense it, and they are verified before posting.[[57]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/IMDb_(identifier)#cite_note-57) However, credit is not given on specific title or filmography pages to the contributor(s) who have provided information. Conversely, a credited text entry, such as a plot summary, may be corrected for content, grammar, sentence structure, perceived omission or error, by other contributors without having to add their names as co-authors. Due to the time required for processing submitted data or text before it is displayed, IMDb is different from user-contributed projects like [Discogs](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Discogs "Discogs"), or [OpenStreetMap](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/OpenStreetMap "OpenStreetMap"), or Wikipedia, in that contributors cannot add, delete, or modify the data or text on impulse, and the manipulation of data is controlled by IMDb technology and salaried staff.[[58]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/IMDb_(identifier)#cite_note-58)

IMDb has been subject to deliberate additions of false information; in 2012 a spokesperson said: "We make it easy for users and professionals to update much of our content, which is why we have an 'edit page'. The data that is submitted goes through a series of consistency checks before it goes live. Given the sheer volume of the information, occasional mistakes are inevitable, and, when reported, they are promptly fixed. We always welcome corrections."[[59]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/IMDb_(identifier)#cite_note-59)

The Java Movie Database (JMDB)[[60]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/IMDb_(identifier)#cite_note-jmdb-60) is reportedly creating an IMDb_Error.log file that lists all the errors found while processing the IMDb plain text files. A Wiki alternative to IMDb is Open Media Database[[61]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/IMDb_(identifier)#cite_note-61) the content of which is also contributed by users but licensed under a [Creative Commons](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Creative_Commons "Creative Commons") license (CC BY) and the [GFDL](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/GNU_Free_Documentation_License "GNU Free Documentation License"). Since 2007, IMDb has been experimenting with wiki-programmed sections for complete film synopses, parental guides, and FAQs about titles as determined by (and answered by) individual contributors.

### Data format and access

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=IMDb&action=edit&section=15 "Edit section: Data format and access")]

IMDb, unlike other AI-automated queries, does not provide an [API](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Web_API "Web API") for automated queries. However, most of the data can be downloaded as [compressed](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Data_compression "Data compression") plain text files and the information can be extracted using the [command-line interface](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Command-line_interface "Command-line interface") tools provided.[[62]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/IMDb_(identifier)#cite_note-62) There is also a Java-based [graphical user interface](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Graphical_user_interface "Graphical user interface") (GUI) application available that is able to process the compressed plain text files, which allows a search and a display of the information.[[60]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/IMDb_(identifier)#cite_note-jmdb-60) This GUI application supports different languages, but the movie related data are in English, as made available by IMDb. A [Python](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Python_(programming_language) "Python (programming language)") package called IMDbPY (since renamed cinemagoer) can also be used to process the compressed plain text files into a number of different [SQL](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/SQL "SQL") databases, enabling easier access to the entire dataset for searching or data mining.[[63]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/IMDb_(identifier)#cite_note-63)[[64]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/IMDb_(identifier)#cite_note-64)[[65]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/IMDb_(identifier)#cite_note-65)

### Podcasts

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=IMDb&action=edit&section=16 "Edit section: Podcasts")]

On October 21, 2021, the site added the ability to add podcasts (both as series and episodes) as titles to the site, via an IMDb employee announcement on their [Sprinklr](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sprinklr "Sprinklr") forums.[[66]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/IMDb_(identifier)#cite_note-forums_podcasts_1-66)As of December 2022[[update]](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=IMDb&action=edit), the numbers of podcast series stood at 24,778, with podcast episodes at 3,076,386.[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/IMDb_(identifier)#cite_note-stats_2022.12-4)

## IMDb STARmeter Awards

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=IMDb&action=edit&section=17 "Edit section: IMDb STARmeter Awards")]

Annually, **IMDb STARmeter Awards** are presented to industry professionals in various categories. Professionals who have appeared in its annual "top 10 lists" are considered for this award. "IMDb determines its definitive top 10 lists using data from IMDbPro STARmeter rankings, which are based on the actual page views of the more than 200 million monthly visitors to the site."[[67]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/IMDb_(identifier)#cite_note-67) Initially IMDb STARmeter Awards were given in two categories, **IMDb Fan favorite STARmeter Award** and **IMDb Breakout STARmeter Award**.[[68]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/IMDb_(identifier)#cite_note-68) Celebrating 20th anniversary of IMDbPro, it launched **IMDb Icon STARmeter Award**, which is given to prominent artists of the industry who have appeared in the top 10 positions throughout the year.[[69]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/IMDb_(identifier)#cite_note-:0-69)[Salma Hayek](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Salma_Hayek "Salma Hayek") received the inaugural award.[[69]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/IMDb_(identifier)#cite_note-:0-69)

## Legal and policy issues

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=IMDb&action=edit&section=18 "Edit section: Legal and policy issues")]

In 2011, in the case of _[Hoang v. Amazon.com, Inc.](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hoang\_v.\_Amazon.com,\_Inc. "Hoang v. Amazon.com, Inc.")_, IMDb was sued by an anonymous actress for at least [US$](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_States_dollar "United States dollar")1,075,000 because the movie website publicly disclosed her age (40, at the time) without her consent.[[70]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/IMDb_(identifier)#cite_note-70) The actress claimed that revealing her age could cause her to lose acting opportunities.[[71]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/IMDb_(identifier)#cite_note-71) Judge [Marsha J. Pechman](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Marsha_J._Pechman "Marsha J. Pechman"), a US district judge in Seattle, dismissed the lawsuit, saying the actress had no grounds to proceed with an anonymous complaint. The actress re-filed and so revealed that she was Huong Hoang of Texas, who uses the stage name Junie Hoang.[[72]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/IMDb_(identifier)#cite_note-72) In 2013, Pechman dismissed all causes of action except for a [breach of contract](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Breach_of_contract "Breach of contract") claim against IMDb; a jury then sided with IMDb on that claim.[[73]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/IMDb_(identifier)#cite_note-73) The [Court of Appeals for the Ninth Circuit](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Court_of_Appeals_for_the_Ninth_Circuit "Court of Appeals for the Ninth Circuit") affirmed the district court judgment in March 2015.[[74]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/IMDb_(identifier)#cite_note-74)

Also in 2011, in the case of _United Video Properties Inc., et al. v. Amazon.Com Inc. et al._,[[75]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/IMDb_(identifier)#cite_note-75) IMDb and Amazon were sued by [Rovi Corporation](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rovi_Corporation "Rovi Corporation") and others for patent infringement over their various program listing offerings.[[76]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/IMDb_(identifier)#cite_note-76) The patent claims were ultimately construed in a way favorable to IMDb, and Rovi / United Video Properties lost the case.[[77]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/IMDb_(identifier)#cite_note-77) In April 2014, the decision was affirmed by the U.S. Court of Appeals for the Federal Circuit.[[78]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/IMDb_(identifier)#cite_note-78)

In January 2017, the State of California enacted state bill AB-1687, a [SAG-AFTRA](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/SAG-AFTRA "SAG-AFTRA")-backed anti-ageism statute which requires "commercial online entertainment employment services" to honor requests by their subscribers for their ages and birthdays to be hidden.[[79]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/IMDb_(identifier)#cite_note-thr-imdblaw-79) By the beginning of 2017, IMDb had received more than 2,300 requests from individuals to remove their date of birth from the site. Included in this group were 10 [Academy Award](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Academy_Award "Academy Award") winners and another 71 nominated for Oscars, [Emmys](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Emmy_Award "Emmy Award"), or [Golden Globes](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Golden_Globe_Award "Golden Globe Award").[[80]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/IMDb_(identifier)#cite_note-80) On February 23, 2017, Judge [Vince Girdhari Chhabria](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Vince_Chhabria "Vince Chhabria") issued a stay on the bill pending a further trial, on the ground that it possibly violated the [First Amendment](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/First_Amendment_to_the_United_States_Constitution "First Amendment to the United States Constitution") because it inhibited the public consumption of information. He also questioned the intent of the bill, as it was ostensibly meant to target IMDb.[[81]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/IMDb_(identifier)#cite_note-thr-lawstruck-81) In February 2018, Chhabria struck down the statute,[[82]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/IMDb_(identifier)#cite_note-82) and in June 2020, the [Ninth Circuit](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ninth_Circuit "Ninth Circuit") affirmed Chhabria's judgement, holding that the statute was an unconstitutional content-based restriction that violated the First Amendment.[[83]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/IMDb_(identifier)#cite_note-83)[[84]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/IMDb_(identifier)#cite_note-84)

IMDb had long maintained that it would keep all valid information, but changed that policy related to birth names in 2019, instead removing birth names that are not widely and publicly known, of persons who no longer use their birth names.[[85]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/IMDb_(identifier)#cite_note-Variety_20190813-85) This was done in response to pressure from [LGBTQ](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/LGBTQ "LGBTQ") groups against the publication of the birth names of [transgender](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Transgender "Transgender") people without their consent ([deadnaming](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Deadnaming "Deadnaming")). Any name a person had previously been credited under, however, continues to be maintained in the credits section, mentioning both the name the person uses and the name appearing in the credits.[[85]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/IMDb_(identifier)#cite_note-Variety_20190813-85)

**Javed Akhtar**[[a]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Javed_Akhtar#cite_note-2) (Urdu pronunciation:[[d͡ʒɑːʋɛd̪əxt̪əɾ]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Help:IPA/Hindi_and_Urdu "Help:IPA/Hindi and Urdu"); born 17 January 1945) is an Indian [screenwriter](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Screenwriter "Screenwriter"), [lyricist](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lyricist "Lyricist"), [poet](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Poet "Poet"), and [political activist](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Political_activist "Political activist"). Renowned for his extensive work in [Hindi cinema](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hindi_cinema "Hindi cinema"), he has won five [National Film Awards](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/National_Film_Awards "National Film Awards") and sixteen [Filmfare Awards](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Filmfare_Awards "Filmfare Awards").[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Javed_Akhtar#cite_note-FilmfareAwards-1) He was honoured with the [Padma Shri](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Padma_Shri "Padma Shri") in 1999 and the [Padma Bhushan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Padma_Bhushan "Padma Bhushan") in 2007,[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Javed_Akhtar#cite_note-Padma_Awards-3) two of India's highest civilian honours. He is widely regarded as one of the greatest screenwriters and lyricists in the history of [Indian cinema](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Indian_cinema "Indian cinema").

Akhtar first gained prominence as one half of the screenwriting duo [Salim–Javed](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Salim%E2%80%93Javed "Salim–Javed"), alongside [Salim Khan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Salim_Khan "Salim Khan"). The pair achieved their breakthrough with _[Zanjeer](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Zanjeer\_(1973\_film) "Zanjeer (1973 film)")_ (1973) and went on to pen several landmark films, including _[Deewaar](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Deewaar "Deewaar")_ (1975) and _[Sholay](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sholay "Sholay")_ (1975). These works achieved cult status and had a lasting influence on Indian popular culture, particularly through their portrayal of the "[angry young man](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Angry_young_man_(India) "Angry young man (India)")" archetype. Following the duo’s split in the early 1980s, Akhtar transitioned into lyric writing, earning acclaim for his poetic and socially conscious lyrics.

In addition to his film career, Akhtar has been an outspoken public intellectual and activist, known for his advocacy of secularism, freedom of expression, and gender equality. He has written and spoken extensively on issues of religion, human rights, and rationalism. Akhtar served as a nominated member of the [Rajya Sabha](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rajya_Sabha "Rajya Sabha") from 2010 to 2016, representing the arts.[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Javed_Akhtar#cite_note-4) He also publicly supported the [Communist Party of India](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Communist_Party_of_India "Communist Party of India") (CPI) during the [2019 Indian general election](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2019_Indian_general_election "2019 Indian general election"). For his contributions to literature, film, and free thought, he became the first Indian to receive the [Richard Dawkins Award](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Richard_Dawkins_Award "Richard Dawkins Award") in 2020.[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Javed_Akhtar#cite_note-5)[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Javed_Akhtar#cite_note-centerforinquiry.org-6)[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Javed_Akhtar#cite_note-7)

In 2024, [Amazon Prime Video](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Amazon_Prime_Video "Amazon Prime Video") released a three-part documentary series titled _[Angry Young Men](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Angry\_Young\_Men\_(miniseries) "Angry Young Men (miniseries)")_, focusing on the partnership between Salim Khan and Javed Akhtar. The documentary explores their creative process, personal relationship, and the enduring impact of their films on Indian cinema.[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Javed_Akhtar#cite_note-8)

In December 2025, Akhtar participated in a public philosophical debate titled _Does God Exist?_ at the [Constitution Club of India](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Constitution_Club_of_India "Constitution Club of India"), New Delhi, where he discussed questions of faith, morality, and human suffering with Islamic scholar [Shamail Nadwi](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shamail_Nadwi "Shamail Nadwi"). Approaching the issue from an atheist perspective, Akhtar questioned the idea of divine justice, particularly in the context of civilian suffering in conflict zones. The debate attracted wide media coverage and public discussion in India and abroad.[[8]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Javed_Akhtar#cite_note-IndiaToday-9)[[9]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Javed_Akhtar#cite_note-IE1-10)[[10]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Javed_Akhtar#cite_note-BBCUrdu-11)

## Early life

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Javed_Akhtar&action=edit&section=1 "Edit section: Early life")]

[![Image 6](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/e/ed/Javed_Akhtar_at_the_2025_Jaipur_Literature_Festival.jpg/250px-Javed_Akhtar_at_the_2025_Jaipur_Literature_Festival.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Javed_Akhtar_at_the_2025_Jaipur_Literature_Festival.jpg)

Javed Akhtar in 2025

Javed Akhtar was born in 1945 in [Gwalior](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gwalior "Gwalior").[[11]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Javed_Akhtar#cite_note-12) His father [Jan Nisar Akhtar](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jan_Nisar_Akhtar "Jan Nisar Akhtar") was a songwriter in [Hindi films](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hindi_cinema "Hindi cinema") and an [Urdu](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Urdu "Urdu") poet.[[12]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Javed_Akhtar#cite_note-13) His paternal grandfather [Muztar Khairabadi](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Muztar_Khairabadi "Muztar Khairabadi") was a poet as was his grandfather's elder brother, Bismil Khairabadi, while his great great grandfather, [Fazl-e-Haq Khairabadi](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fazl-e-Haq_Khairabadi "Fazl-e-Haq Khairabadi"), was a religious scholar of Islam.[[13]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Javed_Akhtar#cite_note-14) Javed Akhtar's original name was Jadoo, taken from a line in a poem written by his father: "Lamha, lamha kisi jadoo ka fasana hoga". He was given the official name of Javed since it was close to the word _jadoo_.[[14]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Javed_Akhtar#cite_note-Chopra-15) He spent most of his childhood and was schooled in [Lucknow](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lucknow "Lucknow"). He graduated from Saifiya College in [Bhopal](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bhopal "Bhopal").[[15]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Javed_Akhtar#cite_note-16)

## Career as scriptwriter

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Javed_Akhtar&action=edit&section=2 "Edit section: Career as scriptwriter")]

Main article: [Salim-Javed](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Salim-Javed "Salim-Javed")

Initially, in the 1970s, there was generally no concept of having the same writer for the screenplay, story and dialogue, nor were the writers given any credits in the titles. [Rajesh Khanna](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rajesh_Khanna "Rajesh Khanna") is credited with giving [Salim Khan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Salim_Khan "Salim Khan") and Javed Akhtar their first chance to become screenplay writers by offering them work in _[Haathi Mere Saathi](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Haathi\_Mere\_Saathi\_(1971\_film) "Haathi Mere Saathi (1971 film)")_.[[16]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Javed_Akhtar#cite_note-17) Javed Akhtar stated in an interview that one day, he went to [Salimsaab](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Salim_Khan "Salim Khan") and said that Mr. Devar had given him a huge signing amount with which he could complete the payment for his bungalow, Aashirwad. But the film was a remake and the script of the original was far from being satisfactory. "He told us that if we could set right the script, he would make sure we got both money and credit."[[17]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Javed_Akhtar#cite_note-18)

Their first big success was the script for _[Andaz](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Andaz\_(1971\_film) "Andaz (1971 film)")_ (1971), followed by _[Haathi Mere Saathi](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Haathi\_Mere\_Saathi\_(1971\_film) "Haathi Mere Saathi (1971 film)")_ (1971) and _[Seeta Aur Geeta](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Seeta\_Aur\_Geeta "Seeta Aur Geeta")_ (1972). They also had hits with _[Yaadon Ki Baaraat](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Yaadon\_Ki\_Baaraat "Yaadon Ki Baaraat")_ (1973), _[Zanjeer](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Zanjeer\_(1973\_film) "Zanjeer (1973 film)")_ (1973), _[Haath Ki Safai](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Haath\_Ki\_Safai "Haath Ki Safai")_ (1974), _[Deewaar](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Deewaar "Deewaar")_ (1975), _[Sholay](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sholay "Sholay")_ (1975), _[Chacha Bhatija](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chacha\_Bhatija "Chacha Bhatija")_ (1977), _[Don](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Don\_(1978\_film) "Don (1978 film)")_ (1978), _[Trishul](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Trishul\_(film) "Trishul (film)")_ (1978), _[Dostana](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dostana\_(1980\_film) "Dostana (1980 film)")_ (1980), _[Kranti](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kranti "Kranti")_ (1981), _[Zamana](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Zamana\_(1985\_film) "Zamana (1985 film)")_ (1985) and _[Mr. India](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mr.\_India\_(1987\_film) "Mr. India (1987 film)")_ (1987). They have worked together in 24 films including two [Kannada](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kannada "Kannada") films – _[Premada Kanike](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Premada\_Kanike "Premada Kanike")_ and _[Raja Nanna Raja](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Raja\_Nanna\_Raja "Raja Nanna Raja")_.

Of the 24 films they wrote, 20 were hits. Their scripts which were not successful at box office include _[Adhikar](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Adhikar\_(1971\_film) "Adhikar (1971 film)")_ (1971), _[Aakhri Dao](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Aakhri\_Daao "Aakhri Daao")_ (1975), _[Immaan Dharam](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Immaan\_Dharam "Immaan Dharam")_ (1977) and _[Shaan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shaan\_(1980\_film) "Shaan (1980 film)")_ (1980). Though they split in 1982, due to ego issues, some of the scripts they wrote were made into hit films later, such as _[Zamana](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Zamaana\_Deewana "Zamaana Deewana")_ and _[Mr. India](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mr.\_India\_(1987\_film) "Mr. India (1987 film)")_. Salim-Javed, many a time described as "the most successful scriptwriters of all-time",[[18]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Javed_Akhtar#cite_note-19) are also noted to be the first scriptwriters in [Indian cinema](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cinema_of_India "Cinema of India") to achieve star status.[[19]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Javed_Akhtar#cite_note-20)

## Personal life

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Javed_Akhtar&action=edit&section=3 "Edit section: Personal life")]

> “There are certain things that I’d like to make clear at the very outset. Don’t get carried away by my name — Javed Akhtar. I am not revealing a secret, I am saying something that I have said many times, in writing or on TV, in public… I’m an atheist, I have no religious beliefs. And I don’t believe in spirituality of some kind".[[20]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Javed_Akhtar#cite_note-21)

Akhtar was nominated to the Parliament upper house [Rajya Sabha](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rajya_Sabha "Rajya Sabha") on 16 November 2009.[[21]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Javed_Akhtar#cite_note-22) Akhtar was married to [Honey Irani](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Honey_Irani "Honey Irani"), with whom he had two children, [Farhan Akhtar](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Farhan_Akhtar "Farhan Akhtar"), a film actor, producer, director[[22]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Javed_Akhtar#cite_note-23) and [Zoya Akhtar](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Zoya_Akhtar "Zoya Akhtar"), a film writer, director and producer.[[23]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Javed_Akhtar#cite_note-24) The father-and-son duo have worked together in films such as _[Dil Chahta Hai](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dil\_Chahta\_Hai "Dil Chahta Hai")_, _[Lakshya](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lakshya\_(2004\_film) "Lakshya (2004 film)")_, _[Rock On!!](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rock\_On!! "Rock On!!")_ and _[Zindagi Na Milegi Dobara](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Zindagi\_Na\_Milegi\_Dobara "Zindagi Na Milegi Dobara")_ with [Zoya](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Zoya_Akhtar "Zoya Akhtar"). [Farhan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Farhan_Akhtar "Farhan Akhtar") was previously married to hair stylist [Adhuna Akhtar](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Adhuna_Akhtar "Adhuna Akhtar"),[[24]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Javed_Akhtar#cite_note-25) they divorced in 2017, and he is currently married to actress and singer [Shibani Dandekar](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shibani_Dandekar "Shibani Dandekar").[[25]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Javed_Akhtar#cite_note-26)

Despite having an Islamic upbringing, Akhtar declared himself to be an "equal opportunity [atheist](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Atheist "Atheist")" who is against all faiths,[[26]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Javed_Akhtar#cite_note-27)[[27]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Javed_Akhtar#cite_note-28) and also brought up his children [Farhan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Farhan_Akhtar "Farhan Akhtar") and [Zoya Akhtar](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Zoya_Akhtar "Zoya Akhtar") as atheists.[[28]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Javed_Akhtar#cite_note-29) However, he continues to identify as a "[cultural Muslim](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cultural_Muslims "Cultural Muslims")" because of his heritage associated with the [Islamic civilization](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Islamic_culture "Islamic culture").[[29]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Javed_Akhtar#cite_note-30)[[30]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Javed_Akhtar#cite_note-31)

Akhtar married [Shabana Azmi](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shabana_Azmi "Shabana Azmi"), the daughter of Urdu poet, [Kaifi Azmi](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kaifi_Azmi "Kaifi Azmi") and later divorced [Irani](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Honey_Irani "Honey Irani").[[31]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Javed_Akhtar#cite_note-32) Akhtar's uncle, Asrar-ul-Haq "[Majaz](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Majaz "Majaz")" was also an Urdu poet. His uncle, [Ansar Harvani](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ansar_Harvani "Ansar Harvani"), was a member of the Indian independence movement and an elected Member of Parliament. Akhtar's aunt, [Hamida Salim](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hamida_Salim "Hamida Salim"), was an Indian author, economist and educator as well.[[32]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Javed_Akhtar#cite_note-33)

Javed was awarded the civilian honour of [Padma Shri](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Padma_Shri "Padma Shri") by the Government of India in 1999, followed by the [Padma Bhushan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Padma_Bhushan "Padma Bhushan") in 2007.[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Javed_Akhtar#cite_note-Padma_Awards-3) In 2013, he received the [Sahitya Akademi Award](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sahitya_Akademi_Award "Sahitya Akademi Award") in [Urdu](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_Sahitya_Akademi_Award_winners_for_Urdu "List of Sahitya Akademi Award winners for Urdu"), India's second highest literary honour, for his poetry collection _Lava_.[[33]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Javed_Akhtar#cite_note-34) In 2019, he was conferred with an [honorary doctorate](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Honorary_doctorate "Honorary doctorate") ([Doctor of Letters](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/D.Litt "D.Litt")) by the [Jamia Hamdard University](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jamia_Hamdard "Jamia Hamdard").[[34]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Javed_Akhtar#cite_note-35) In 2020 he was awarded the [Richard Dawkins Award](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Richard_Dawkins_Award "Richard Dawkins Award") for being a "powerful force for secularism, reason, and human rights, challenging superstition and intolerance through his work in poetry, screenwriting, and political activism". [![Image 39: E. M. Forster A Passage to #India (1924) Here is the full text of the #famous #opening passage: On the second rise is laid out the little civil station, and viewed hence Chandrapore appears to be a totally different place. It is a city of gardens. It is no city, but a forest sparsely scattered with huts. It is a tropical pleasaunce washed by a noble river. The toddy palms and neem trees and mangoes and pepul that were hidden behind the bazaars now become visible and in their turn hide the bazaars. Each person who knew her—her sister, her lover, a troubled young man, a jealous wife, and a local boy—presents a drastically different version of her personality, shifting her from kind to cruel, glamorous to manipulative, victim to villain. The police must navigate these contradictory narratives to uncover who Agnes truly was and who had the strongest motive to kill her. The film’s Rashomon‑style structure makes every character unreliable, and the shifting tone—from melodrama to noir to domestic tension—creates a layered portrait of a woman seen only through the distortions of others. Fans of anthology‑style mysteries or multi‑perspective crime dramas often seek this film out, and it is frequently recommended alongside other British noir titles of the era such as Green for Danger and Cast a Dark Shadow. The U.S. title Five Angles on Murder was chosen to emphasize the film’s structure rather than its original fortune‑teller theme. 6. The production used a modest budget typical of Rank Organisation mid‑tier releases, relying heavily on performance and narrative rather than elaborate sets. 7. Many scenes were shot on controlled studio stages to allow lighting changes between perspectives without continuity issues. 8. Jean Kent’s wardrobe was intentionally inconsistent—each witness imagined her differently, so costuming varied from glamorous to plain. 9. The film’s nonlinear editing was considered innovative and required unusually close collaboration between Asquith and editor Gerald Turney‑Smith. 10. # Nasir Hussain facts for kids

[Kids Encyclopedia Facts](https://kids.kiddle.co/)

This page is about the film producer. For the cricketer, see Nasser Hussain. For the actor, see Nazir Hussain.

| Quick facts for kids Nasir Husain |
| --- |
| [![Image 3: Nasir Hussain Director.jpg](https://kids.kiddle.co/images/thumb/b/bd/Nasir_Hussain_Director.jpg/300px-Nasir_Hussain_Director.jpg)](https://kids.kiddle.co/Image:Nasir_Hussain_Director.jpg) |
| Born | 16 November 1926 [Bhopal](https://kids.kiddle.co/Bhopal "Bhopal"), [Bhopal State](https://kids.kiddle.co/Bhopal_State "Bhopal State"), [British India](https://kids.kiddle.co/British_India "British India") |
| Died | 13 March 2002(2002-03-13) (aged 75) [Mumbai](https://kids.kiddle.co/Mumbai "Mumbai"), [Maharashtra](https://kids.kiddle.co/Maharashtra "Maharashtra"), [India](https://kids.kiddle.co/India "India") |
| Occupation | [Director](https://kids.kiddle.co/Movie_director "Movie director"), [Producer](https://kids.kiddle.co/Movie_producer "Movie producer"), [Screenwriter](https://kids.kiddle.co/Screenwriter "Screenwriter") |
| Years active | 1948–1996 |
| Spouse(s) | Ayesha Khan |
| Children | Mansoor Khan Nuzhat Khan |
| Relatives | Tahir Hussain (brother) Tariq Khan (nephew) [Aamir Khan](https://kids.kiddle.co/Aamir_Khan "Aamir Khan") (nephew) [Faisal Khan](https://kids.kiddle.co/Faisal_Khan "Faisal Khan") (nephew) Imran Khan (grandson) |

**Mohammad Nasir Hussain Khan**, also known as **Nasir Hussain** (born November 16, 1926 – died March 13, 2002), was a very important Indian film producer, director, and writer. He had a long career and is remembered for setting big trends in the history of [Hindi cinema](https://kids.kiddle.co/Bollywood "Bollywood"). For example, he directed _Yaadon Ki Baraat_ (1973), which created the "masala film" style. This style mixed action, comedy, and romance, and was very popular in the 1970s and 1980s. He also wrote and produced _[Qayamat Se Qayamat Tak](https://kids.kiddle.co/Qayamat\_Se\_Qayamat\_Tak "Qayamat Se Qayamat Tak")_ (1988). This movie set the standard for musical romance films in the 1990s. A book about his films, called _Music, Masti, Modernity: The Cinema of Nasir Husain_, was written by Akshay Manwani.

## Contents

*   [Nasir Hussain's Film Journey](https://kids.kiddle.co/Nasir_Hussain#Nasir_Hussain.27s_Film_Journey)
    *   [Starting His Career](https://kids.kiddle.co/Nasir_Hussain#Starting_His_Career)
    *   [Becoming a Producer and Director](https://kids.kiddle.co/Nasir_Hussain#Becoming_a_Producer_and_Director)
    *   [Later Years and Legacy](https://kids.kiddle.co/Nasir_Hussain#Later_Years_and_Legacy)

*   [Collaborations and Associations](https://kids.kiddle.co/Nasir_Hussain#Collaborations_and_Associations)
*   [Awards and Recognitions](https://kids.kiddle.co/Nasir_Hussain#Awards_and_Recognitions)
*   [Filmography](https://kids.kiddle.co/Nasir_Hussain#Filmography)

## Nasir Hussain's Film Journey

### Starting His Career

Nasir Hussain began his film career in 1948. He joined a film studio called Filmistan as a writer. He wrote many famous films for them, including _Anarkali_ (1953), _Munimji_ (1955), and _Paying Guest_ (1957). Filmistan was known for making movies with good music and popular stars.

Sashadhar Mukherjee, a key person at Filmistan, gave Hussain his first chance to direct. This was for the film _Tumsa Nahin Dekha_. This movie helped make [Shammi Kapoor](https://kids.kiddle.co/Shammi_Kapoor "Shammi Kapoor") a big star. Hussain and Kapoor then made another hit film, _Dil Deke Dekho_ (1959). This movie also introduced [Asha Parekh](https://kids.kiddle.co/Asha_Parekh "Asha Parekh"), who became a lead actress in many of Hussain's films.

### Becoming a Producer and Director

After working for other studios, Nasir Hussain started his own company, Nasir Hussain Films. He became a producer and director, making many musical hits. Some of these popular films include _Jab Pyar Kisi Se Hota Hai_ (1961), _Phir Wohi Dil Laya Hoon_ (1963), _Teesri Manzil_ (1966), and _Caravan_ (1971).

He often worked with the lyricist [Majrooh Sultanpuri](https://kids.kiddle.co/Majrooh_Sultanpuri "Majrooh Sultanpuri") and the music composer [R.D. Burman](https://kids.kiddle.co/R._D._Burman "R. D. Burman"). They created many memorable songs together. Their collaborations included _Teesri Manzil_, _Caravan_, and _Yaadon Ki Baraat_.

Hussain wrote and produced the popular musical film _Teesri Manzil_. [Vijay Anand](https://kids.kiddle.co/Vijay_Anand_(filmmaker) "Vijay Anand (filmmaker)") directed it, and it starred Shammi Kapoor and Asha Parekh. For this film, Hussain hired [R.D. Burman](https://kids.kiddle.co/R._D._Burman "R. D. Burman") to compose the music for the first time. The songs became huge hits. After this success, Burman composed music for all of Hussain's films for the next 19 years.

His film _Yaadon Ki Baraat_ (1973) was written by the famous duo Salim–Javed. This movie is known as the first "masala film." It mixed different genres like action, comedy, and romance, which became a very popular style in Bollywood.

### Later Years and Legacy

In the 1980s, some of Hussain's films like _Zamane Ko Dikhana Hai_ (1981) and _Zabardast_ (1985) were not as successful. His son, Mansoor Khan, then took over the main directing roles at Nasir Hussain Films. However, Nasir Hussain continued to write scripts.

He wrote the scripts for important films like _[Qayamat Se Qayamat Tak](https://kids.kiddle.co/Qayamat\_Se\_Qayamat\_Tak "Qayamat Se Qayamat Tak")_ (1988) and _[Jo Jeeta Wohi Sikander](https://kids.kiddle.co/Jo\_Jeeta\_Wohi\_Sikandar "Jo Jeeta Wohi Sikandar")_ (1992). In _Qayamat Se Qayamat Tak_, he introduced his nephew, [Aamir Khan](https://kids.kiddle.co/Aamir_Khan "Aamir Khan"), as a hero. This film was a major turning point in Hindi cinema. It set the standard for Bollywood musical romance films that were very popular throughout the 1990s.

In 1996, Nasir Hussain received a special Filmfare Award. This award recognized his huge contributions to Hindi cinema.

Nasir Hussain passed away in Mumbai on March 13, 2002, after a heart attack. He left behind a great legacy of films that shaped Bollywood.

## Collaborations and Associations

Nasir Hussain often worked with the same talented people on many of his films.

*   He started his career working with Sashadhar Mukherjee at Filmistan Studio.
*   He cast [Dev Anand](https://kids.kiddle.co/Dev_Anand "Dev Anand") in his first film as a producer, _Jab Pyar Kisi Se Hota Hai_.
*   The actor [Pran](https://kids.kiddle.co/Pran_(actor) "Pran (actor)") often played the villain in his films.
*   [Shammi Kapoor](https://kids.kiddle.co/Shammi_Kapoor "Shammi Kapoor") starred in many of his early hits, and Hussain helped create Kapoor's famous energetic image.
*   Actor Rajindernath appeared in almost all of Hussain's early productions, bringing comedy to the screen.
*   His longest collaboration was with leading lady [Asha Parekh](https://kids.kiddle.co/Asha_Parekh "Asha Parekh"). She starred in many of his films, from _Dil Deke Dekho_ to _Caravan_.
*   He worked with music composer [R.D. Burman](https://kids.kiddle.co/R._D._Burman "R. D. Burman") on 9 films, creating many classic songs.
*   His wife, Ayesha Khan, also worked as an assistant choreographer on some of his productions.

## Awards and Recognitions

Nasir Hussain received several important awards for his work:

*   Filmfare Best Movie Award - _[Qayamat Se Qayamat Tak](https://kids.kiddle.co/Qayamat\_Se\_Qayamat\_Tak "Qayamat Se Qayamat Tak")_ (1988)
*   Filmfare Best Screenplay Award - _[Qayamat Se Qayamat Tak](https://kids.kiddle.co/Qayamat\_Se\_Qayamat\_Tak "Qayamat Se Qayamat Tak")_ (1988)
*   Filmfare Best Movie Award – _[Jo Jeeta Wohi Sikandar](https://kids.kiddle.co/Jo\_Jeeta\_Wohi\_Sikandar "Jo Jeeta Wohi Sikandar")_ (1992)
*   Filmfare Special Award (1996)

He was a director and producer, known for [Veerapandiya Kattabomman (1959)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt0250803/?ls), [Thangamalai Rahasyam (1957)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt0250775/?ls) and [Karnan (1964)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt0250461/?ls). [Deiva Magan (1969)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt1437598/?ref_=ls_knf_3)

A. C. Tirulokachandar was an Indian film director and screenwriter who worked mainly in Tamil films from the 1960s to 1988. He also directed a few films in Hindi and Telugu. His 1969 Tamil film Deiva Magan was the first South Indian film to be submitted by India in a contest for the Academy Award for Best Foreign Language Film. He directed the pair Sivaji Ganeshan and Jayalalitha in 5 films - Deiva Magan, Dharmam Engey, Engirundho Vandhaal, Enga Mama, Avanthan Manidhan. He directed Rajesh Khanna in Babu in 1985 which became a hit.
