# Qayamat Se Qayamat Tak facts for kids

[Kids Encyclopedia Facts](https://kids.kiddle.co/)

| Quick facts for kids Qayamat Se Qayamat Tak |
| --- |
| Directed by | Mansoor Khan |
| Produced by | [Nasir Hussain](https://kids.kiddle.co/Nasir_Hussain "Nasir Hussain") |
| Written by | [Nasir Hussain](https://kids.kiddle.co/Nasir_Hussain "Nasir Hussain") |
| Starring | [Aamir Khan](https://kids.kiddle.co/Aamir_Khan "Aamir Khan") [Juhi Chawla](https://kids.kiddle.co/Juhi_Chawla "Juhi Chawla") |
| Music by | Anand-Milind |
| Cinematography | Kiran Deohans |
| Editing by | Zafar Sultan |
| Distributed by | Nasir Hussain Films |
| Release date(s) | 23 April 1988 |
| Running time | 163 mins |
| Country | India |
| Language | [Hindi](https://kids.kiddle.co/Hindi_language "Hindi language") |

_**Qayamat Se Qayamat Tak**_ or _**QSQT**_ (which means "From Resurrection to Resurrection" in English) is a super popular [Bollywood](https://kids.kiddle.co/Bollywood "Bollywood") romantic movie from 1988. It was directed by Mansoor Khan. The movie stars [Aamir Khan](https://kids.kiddle.co/Aamir_Khan "Aamir Khan") and [Juhi Chawla](https://kids.kiddle.co/Juhi_Chawla "Juhi Chawla"), who became very famous after this film! The story is a modern Indian version of the classic play _[Romeo and Juliet](https://kids.kiddle.co/Romeo\_and\_Juliet "Romeo and Juliet")_, but with its own unique twists. It's a tale about two young people from rival families who fall in love.

## Contents

*   [About the Movie](https://kids.kiddle.co/Qayamat_Se_Qayamat_Tak#About_the_Movie)
    *   [The Story](https://kids.kiddle.co/Qayamat_Se_Qayamat_Tak#The_Story)
    *   [Main Characters](https://kids.kiddle.co/Qayamat_Se_Qayamat_Tak#Main_Characters)

*   [The Music](https://kids.kiddle.co/Qayamat_Se_Qayamat_Tak#The_Music)

## About the Movie

_Qayamat Se Qayamat Tak_ is often called a "classic" in Indian cinema. It brought a fresh, youthful feel to [Bollywood](https://kids.kiddle.co/Bollywood "Bollywood") movies. The film was a huge success and helped launch the careers of its main stars, [Aamir Khan](https://kids.kiddle.co/Aamir_Khan "Aamir Khan") and [Juhi Chawla](https://kids.kiddle.co/Juhi_Chawla "Juhi Chawla"). It's known for its beautiful music, touching story, and memorable performances.

### The Story

The movie tells the story of Raj and Rashmi. They come from two families, the Singhs and the Khans, who are bitter enemies. Their families have a long-standing feud. Despite this, Raj and Rashmi meet and fall deeply in love. Their love story faces many challenges because of their families' hatred. The film explores themes of love, family loyalty, and overcoming obstacles.

### Main Characters

*   [Aamir Khan](https://kids.kiddle.co/Aamir_Khan "Aamir Khan") as Raj: A young, charming boy from the Khan family. He falls in love with Rashmi.
*   [Juhi Chawla](https://kids.kiddle.co/Juhi_Chawla "Juhi Chawla") as Rashmi: A beautiful and strong-willed girl from the rival Singh family. She loves Raj deeply.
*   Goga Kapoor as Randhir Singh: Rashmi's strict and powerful father.
*   Dalip Tahil as Dhanraj Singh: Raj's father, who is also part of the family feud.
*   Alok Nath as Jaswant Singh: Another important family member.
*   [Reema Lagoo](https://kids.kiddle.co/Reema_Lagoo "Reema Lagoo") as Mrs. Kamla Singh: A kind character in the story.

## The Music

The music of _Qayamat Se Qayamat Tak_ was a huge hit! The songs were composed by Anand-Milind and are still loved today. Many of the songs became very popular and are considered classics. They helped make the movie even more special.

# Vijay Anand (filmmaker) facts for kids

[Kids Encyclopedia Facts](https://kids.kiddle.co/)

For the Indian politician, see Vijay Anand (politician).

| Quick facts for kids Vijay Anand |
| --- |
| [![Image 3: Vijay Anand in the film Agra Road.jpg](https://kids.kiddle.co/images/0/0b/Vijay_Anand_in_the_film_Agra_Road.jpg)](https://kids.kiddle.co/Image:Vijay_Anand_in_the_film_Agra_Road.jpg) Vijay Anand in _Agra Road_ (1957) |
| Born | (1934-01-22)22 January 1934 Gurdaspur, Punjab, [British India](https://kids.kiddle.co/British_Raj "British Raj") (present-day [Punjab](https://kids.kiddle.co/Punjab_(India) "Punjab (India)"), [India](https://kids.kiddle.co/India "India")) |
| Died | 23 February 2004(2004-02-23) (aged 70) [Mumbai](https://kids.kiddle.co/Mumbai "Mumbai"), [Maharashtra](https://kids.kiddle.co/Maharashtra "Maharashtra"), [India](https://kids.kiddle.co/India "India") |
| Other names | Goldie |
| Relatives | See Anand-Sahni family |
| Awards | Filmfare Best Director Award:_Guide_ (1965) Filmfare Best Dialogue Award: _Guide_ (1965) Filmfare Best Editing Award: _Johnny Mera Naam_ (1970) |

**Vijay Anand** (born January 22, 1934 – died February 23, 2004) was a famous [Indian](https://kids.kiddle.co/Bollywood "Bollywood") filmmaker. People also knew him as **Goldie Anand**. He was a director, producer, writer, editor, and actor. He is best known for popular films like _Guide_ (1965), _Teesri Manzil_ (1966), _Jewel Thief_ (1967), and _Johny Mera Naam_ (1970). Most of his movies were made under the company Navketan Films, which his family owned. He was part of the well-known Anand family in the film industry.

## Contents

*   [About His Life](https://kids.kiddle.co/Vijay_Anand_(filmmaker)#About_His_Life)
*   [His Film Career](https://kids.kiddle.co/Vijay_Anand_(filmmaker)#His_Film_Career)
    *   [Top Movies He Directed](https://kids.kiddle.co/Vijay_Anand_(filmmaker)#Top_Movies_He_Directed)
    *   [His Acting Roles](https://kids.kiddle.co/Vijay_Anand_(filmmaker)#His_Acting_Roles)

*   [Filmography](https://kids.kiddle.co/Vijay_Anand_(filmmaker)#Filmography)
    *   [Director](https://kids.kiddle.co/Vijay_Anand_(filmmaker)#Director)
    *   [Writer](https://kids.kiddle.co/Vijay_Anand_(filmmaker)#Writer)
    *   [Actor](https://kids.kiddle.co/Vijay_Anand_(filmmaker)#Actor)

*   [His Legacy](https://kids.kiddle.co/Vijay_Anand_(filmmaker)#His_Legacy)
*   [Awards He Won](https://kids.kiddle.co/Vijay_Anand_(filmmaker)#Awards_He_Won)

## About His Life

Vijay Anand was born in Gurdaspur, [Punjab, India](https://kids.kiddle.co/Punjab_(India) "Punjab (India)"). His father, Pishori Lal Anand, was a successful lawyer. Vijay was the youngest of nine children. His older brothers were [Chetan Anand](https://kids.kiddle.co/Chetan_Anand_(director) "Chetan Anand (director)"), a producer and director, and [Dev Anand](https://kids.kiddle.co/Dev_Anand "Dev Anand"), a very famous actor. His sister, Sheel Kanta Kapur, was the mother of film director [Shekhar Kapur](https://kids.kiddle.co/Shekhar_Kapur "Shekhar Kapur").

Vijay married Sushma Kohli, who was his niece. Their marriage was quite unusual for the time, and some people in society found it surprising. However, Vijay and Sushma had a happy marriage that lasted their whole lives. They had one son together, named Vaibhav Anand.

## His Film Career

Vijay Anand did many things in films, like acting, writing, editing, and producing. But he is mostly remembered as a director. He directed his first movie, _Nau Do Gyarah_, in 1957. It was a big hit! His brother, [Dev Anand](https://kids.kiddle.co/Dev_Anand "Dev Anand"), starred in the film, and it was filmed very quickly, in just 40 days.

### Top Movies He Directed

Vijay directed many other successful movies. Some of these include _Kala Bazar_ (1960), _Guide_ (1965), _Teesri Manzil_ (1966), and _Jewel Thief_ (1967). He also directed _Johny Mera Naam_ (1970), _Tere Mere Sapne_ (1971), _Ram Balram_ (1980), and _[Rajput](https://kids.kiddle.co/Rajput "Rajput")_ (1982).

Most of these films were made by Navketan films. This was a production company started by the Anand brothers themselves. A few movies, like _Teesri Manzil_, _Ram-Balram_, and _Rajput_, were made by other producers. The years from 1957 to 1970 were the most successful time in Vijay Anand's career.

His 1965 film _Guide_ was a huge success. It starred Dev Anand and [Waheeda Rehman](https://kids.kiddle.co/Waheeda_Rehman "Waheeda Rehman"). The movie was based on a book by [R. K. Narayan](https://kids.kiddle.co/R._K._Narayan "R. K. Narayan"). _Guide_ was not only his biggest hit but also praised by critics and loved by audiences and music fans. Navketan Films tried to release an English version of _Guide_ internationally, but it didn't do as well.

Vijay Anand was known for how beautifully he filmed songs in his movies. Some famous examples include "O Haseena Zulfonwali" from _Teesri Manzil_, "Aaj Phir Jeene Ki Tamanna Hai" from _Guide_, and "Honthon Mein Aisi Baat" from _Jewel Thief_.

### His Acting Roles

Vijay Anand also acted in films. He first appeared as an actor in _Agra Road_ (1957). Some of his most memorable acting roles were in movies like _Kala Bazar_ (1960), _Haqeeqat_ (1964), and _Kora Kagaz_ (1974). In _Kora Kagaz_, he acted alongside [Jaya Bachchan](https://kids.kiddle.co/Jaya_Bachchan "Jaya Bachchan"). He also appeared in _Main Tulsi Tere Aangan Ki_ (1978).

He acted with Leena Chandavarkar in the thriller _Chor Chor_ (1974). He also starred with Rekha in _Ghungroo Ki Awaaz_ (1981) and _Double Cross_ (1972). With his brother [Dev Anand](https://kids.kiddle.co/Dev_Anand "Dev Anand"), he acted in _Chhupa Rustam_ (1973) and _Tere Mere Sapne_, which also featured [Hema Malini](https://kids.kiddle.co/Hema_Malini "Hema Malini") and Mumtaz.

Later, in the 1990s, many young people knew him for playing the detective "Sam" in the TV show _Tehkikaat_ (1994).

Vijay Anand also worked for a short time as the head of the Central Board of Film Certification. This board is India's censor board, which checks films before they are released. He left this position in 2002.

Vijay Anand, or Goldie as his friends called him, passed away on February 23, 2004. He was 70 years old and died from a [heart attack](https://kids.kiddle.co/Myocardial_infarction "Myocardial infarction").

## Filmography

### Director

*   _Nau Do Gyarah_ (1957)
*   _Kala Bazar_ (1960)
*   _Tere Ghar Ke Samne_ (1963)
*   _Guide_ (1965)
*   _Teesri Manzil_ (1966)
*   _Jewel Thief_ (1967)
*   _Kahin Aur Chal_ (1968)
*   _Johny Mera Naam_ (1970)
*   _Tere Mere Sapne_ (1971)
*   _Blackmail_ (1973)
*   _Chhupa Rustam_ (1973)
*   _Bullet_ (1976)
*   _Ek Do Teen Chaar_ (1980)
*   _Ram Balram_ (1980)
*   _Rajput_ (1982)
*   _Main Tere Liye_ (1988)

### Writer

*   _Taxi Driver_ (1954)
*   _Hum Dono_ (1961)

### Actor

*   _Agra Road_ (1957) - Sunil
*   _Kala Bazar_ (1960) - Nand Kumar Chattopadhyay
*   _Haqeeqat_ (1964) - Major Pratap Singh
*   _Tere Mere Sapne_ (1971) - Dr. Jagannath Kothari
*   _Double Cross_ (1972) - Ajay Arya / Vijay Arya / Jimmy
*   _Chhupa Rustam_ (1973) - Jimmy Fernandes
*   _Kora Kagaz_ (1974) - Professor Sukesh Dutt
*   _Chor Chor_ (1974) - N/A
*   _Main Tulsi Tere Aangan Ki_ (1978) - Thakur Rajnath Singh Chouhan
*   _Ghungroo Ki Awaaz_ (1981) - Thakur Ranjeet Singh
*   _Tehkikaat_ (1994) - Sam D'Silva

## His Legacy

Vijay Anand's work has inspired other filmmakers. The thriller film _Johnny Gaddar_ by Sriram Raghavan is dedicated to him. It shows how much Vijay Anand influenced Hindi thrillers. In one scene of _Johnny Gaddar_, a character watches Vijay Anand's movie _Johny Mera Naam_ and then uses the name "Johnny" to hide his identity. In another scene, an actor is seen reading the book _The Guide_, which is a nod to one of Vijay Anand's most famous films.

In 2007, a special event was held at the International Film Festival of India (IFFI) in Goa. They showed many of his films to honor his work.

His film _Guide_ has been studied by many writers and thinkers. There is even a book called _Guide the Film Perspectives_ that deeply explores the amazing direction in the movie. He also acted in the TV show _Tehkikaat_ on Delhi Doordarshan.

## Awards He Won

*   Filmfare Award for Best Director for _Guide_ (1965)
*   Filmfare Award for Best Dialogue for _Guide_ (1965)
*   Filmfare Award for Best Screenplay for _Johnny Mera Naam_ (1970)
*   Filmfare Award for Best Editing for _Johnny Mera Naam_ (1970)
*   BFJA Awards as Best Editor for _Johnny Mera Naam_ (1970)
*   BFJA Awards as Best Editor for _Double Cross_ (1972)

# Jo Jeeta Wohi Sikandar facts for kids

_**Jo Jeeta Wohi Sikandar**_ (which means "He who wins is the conqueror") is a popular [Urdu](https://kids.kiddle.co/Urdu "Urdu") language sports drama movie from 1992. Mansoor Khan directed this film. It stars [Aamir Khan](https://kids.kiddle.co/Aamir_Khan "Aamir Khan") and Ayesha Jhulka in the main roles. Other actors like Mamik Singh, Deepak Tijori, Kulbhushan Kharbanda, and Pooja Bedi also have important parts. The movie is about growing up, friendship, and a big bicycle race.

## Meet the Characters

This movie has many interesting characters. They all play a part in the story of friendship and competition.

### Main Actors and Their Roles

*   [Aamir Khan](https://kids.kiddle.co/Aamir_Khan "Aamir Khan") plays **Sanjaylal Sharma**, also known as Sanju. He is a fun-loving student who learns important lessons.
*   Ayesha Jhulka plays **Anjali**. She is Sanju's kind and supportive friend.
*   Deepak Tijori plays **Shekhar Malhotra**. He is a skilled but sometimes arrogant rival in the race.
*   Pooja Bedi plays **Devika**. She is a stylish and confident student.
*   [Kulbhushan Kharbanda](https://kids.kiddle.co/Kulbhushan_Kharbanda "Kulbhushan Kharbanda") plays **Ramlal Sharma**. He is Sanju's father and a loving parent.
*   Mamik Singh plays **Ratanlal Sharma**. He is Sanju's older brother, who is very dedicated.

### Other Important Characters

*   Aditya Lakhia as Maksood, also called Ghode.
*   Deven Bhojani as Ghanshyam, also called Ghanshu.
*   Kiran Zaveri as Kalpana.
*   Asrani as Mr. Dubey, a teacher at Model school.
*   Faisal Khan in a special appearance as a college student.
*   Imran Khan as Young Sanjaylal.
*   Sharokh Bharucha as Young Ratanlal.
*   Anjan Srivastava as a race commentator.
*   Ajit Vachani as Rajput's Principal.
*   Deb Mukherjee as a coach.
*   Jatin Pandit as a performer at the annual college event.
*   Amol Gupte as a cycle race commentator.

Visu was born on 1 July 1945 in British India. He was an actor and writer, known for [Samsaram Athu Minsaram (1986)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt0308840/?ref_=nm_ov_bio_lk), [Neenga Nalla Irukkanum (1992)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt0273877/?ref_=nm_ov_bio_lk) and [Aadhade Adharam (1976)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt8669188/?ref_=nm_ov_bio_lk). He was married to Sundhari. He died on 22 March 2020 in Chennai, Tamil Nadu, India.

Visu was born on 1 July 1945 in British India. He was an actor and writer, known for [Samsaram Athu Minsaram (1986)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt0308840/?ref_=nm_ov_bio_lk), [Neenga Nalla Irukkanum (1992)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt0273877/?ref_=nm_ov_bio_lk) and [Aadhade Adharam (1976)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt8669188/?ref_=nm_ov_bio_lk). He was married to Sundhari. He died on 22 March 2020 in Chennai, Tamil Nadu, India.

Visu was born on 1 July 1945 in British India. He was an actor and writer, known for [Samsaram Athu Minsaram (1986)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt0308840/?ref_=nm_ov_bio_lk), [Neenga Nalla Irukkanum (1992)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt0273877/?ref_=nm_ov_bio_lk) and [Aadhade Adharam (1976)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt8669188/?ref_=nm_ov_bio_lk). He was married to Sundhari. He died on 22 March 2020 in Chennai, Tamil Nadu, India.

**Mohammed Aamir Hussain Khan** (born 14 March 1965) is a famous Indian actor, filmmaker, and TV personality. He works mainly in [Hindi films](https://kids.kiddle.co/Bollywood "Bollywood"). People often call him "Mr. Perfectionist" because he works very hard.

Aamir Khan is known for choosing movies that talk about important social issues. These include topics like education and gender equality. His films often have a positive impact on society in India and other countries. Over his career of more than 30 years, Khan has become one of the most important actors in Indian cinema.

He has won many awards, including nine Filmfare Awards and four [National Film Awards](https://kids.kiddle.co/National_Film_Awards "National Film Awards"). The [Government of India](https://kids.kiddle.co/India "India") honored him with the [Padma Shri](https://kids.kiddle.co/Padma_Shri "Padma Shri") in 2003 and the [Padma Bhushan](https://kids.kiddle.co/Padma_Bhushan "Padma Bhushan") in 2010. He also received an honorary title from the Government of China in 2017.

Aamir Khan first acted as a child in his uncle [Nasir Hussain](https://kids.kiddle.co/Nasir_Hussain "Nasir Hussain")'s film _Yaadon Ki Baaraat_ (1973). As an adult, his first main role was in _Holi_ (1984). He started acting full-time with a leading role in _[Qayamat Se Qayamat Tak](https://kids.kiddle.co/Qayamat\_Se\_Qayamat\_Tak "Qayamat Se Qayamat Tak")_ (1988). His acting in _Raakh_ (1989) earned him a special National Film Award.

In the 1990s, he became a top actor with many successful films. These include _Dil_ (1990), _Rangeela_ (1995), and _[Raja Hindustani](https://kids.kiddle.co/Raja\_Hindustani "Raja Hindustani")_ (1996). For _Raja Hindustani_, he won his first Filmfare Award for Best Actor. He also starred in _Sarfarosh_ (1999).

In 1999, he started his own company, Aamir Khan Productions. Their first film, _Lagaan_ (2001), was nominated for an [Academy Award for Best Foreign Language Film](https://kids.kiddle.co/Academy_Award_for_Best_International_Feature_Film "Academy Award for Best International Feature Film"). It also won him a National Film Award and two more Filmfare Awards. His role in _Dil Chahta Hai_ (2001) was also highly praised. After a break, Khan returned with films like _Rang De Basanti_ (2006) and _Fanaa_ (2006).

He directed his first film, _[Taare Zameen Par](https://kids.kiddle.co/Taare\_Zameen\_Par "Taare Zameen Par")_ (2007). This movie won him Filmfare Awards for Best Film and Best Director. Khan's biggest hits include _Ghajini_ (2008), _3 Idiots_ (2009), _Dhoom 3_ (2013), _PK_ (2014), and _Dangal_ (2016). Each of these films broke records for being the highest-earning Indian film at the time. Khan won his third Best Actor award at Filmfare for _Dangal_.

He has many fans, especially in India and [China](https://kids.kiddle.co/China "China"). _Newsweek_ magazine called him "the biggest movie star in the world." He also created and hosted the TV talk show _Satyamev Jayate_. His work as a social reformer led to him being on the _Time_ 100 list of most influential people in 2013.

## Early Life and Family Background

Mohammed Aamir Hussain Khan was born on 14 March 1965 in [Bombay](https://kids.kiddle.co/Mumbai "Mumbai"). His father, Tahir Hussain, was a film producer, and his mother is Zeenat Hussain. He has three siblings: a younger brother, [Faisal Khan](https://kids.kiddle.co/Faisal_Khan "Faisal Khan"), and two sisters, Farhat and Nikhat Khan.

His family has roots from [Herat](https://kids.kiddle.co/Herat "Herat") in [Afghanistan](https://kids.kiddle.co/Afghanistan "Afghanistan"). Many of his relatives worked in the Hindi film industry. This includes his uncle, producer-director [Nasir Hussain](https://kids.kiddle.co/Nasir_Hussain "Nasir Hussain"). Nasir's son Mansoor Khan is a director who has often cast Aamir in his movies. Nasir's grandson, Imran Khan, is also a former Hindi film actor.

As a child, Aamir appeared in two small movie roles. At age eight, he was in _Yaadon Ki Baaraat_ (1973). This was the first masala film in [Bollywood](https://kids.kiddle.co/Bollywood "Bollywood"). The next year, he played a younger character in _Madhosh_ (1974).

Aamir attended different schools, including J.B. Petit School and Bombay Scottish School, Mahim. He was very good at tennis and became a state-level champion. He said he was "much more into sports than studies." He finished his schooling at Mumbai's Narsee Monjee College. He described his childhood as "tough" because his father's films were not always successful, leading to money problems.

At 16, Khan helped make a 40-minute silent film called _Paranoia_. He played the main role and helped the director. This experience made him want to work in films. He then joined a theater group and acted in several plays. After high school, he decided to work as an assistant director for his uncle.

In 2013, Aamir Khan went on [Hajj](https://kids.kiddle.co/Hajj "Hajj"), a religious trip to [Mecca](https://kids.kiddle.co/Mecca "Mecca"), with his mother.

## Acting Career Highlights

### Early Roles and First Success

Aamir Khan's first major film role was in _Holi_ (1984). He played a college student in this experimental film. Later, his uncle Nasir Hussain and cousin Mansoor Khan cast him in _[Qayamat Se Qayamat Tak](https://kids.kiddle.co/Qayamat\_Se\_Qayamat\_Tak "Qayamat Se Qayamat Tak")_ (1988). He starred opposite [Juhi Chawla](https://kids.kiddle.co/Juhi_Chawla "Juhi Chawla") in this romantic film. The movie was a big hit and made both actors famous. Khan won a Filmfare Award for Best Male Debut.

In 1989, he received a special National Film Award for his acting in both _Qayamat Se Qayamat Tak_ and _Raakh_.

### Becoming a Leading Star

In 1990, Khan had five film releases. His romantic drama _Dil_, co-starring [Madhuri Dixit](https://kids.kiddle.co/Madhuri_Dixit "Madhuri Dixit"), was a huge success. It became the highest-earning film of 1990. He also starred in _Dil Hai Ke Manta Nahin_, which was a hit.

[![Image 4: Aamir Khan at 92.7 BIG FM to promote Satyamev Jayate 07](https://kids.kiddle.co/images/thumb/d/d7/Aamir_Khan_at_92.7_BIG_FM_to_promote_Satyamev_Jayate_07.jpg/140px-Aamir_Khan_at_92.7_BIG_FM_to_promote_Satyamev_Jayate_07.jpg)](https://kids.kiddle.co/Image:Aamir_Khan_at_92.7_BIG_FM_to_promote_Satyamev_Jayate_07.jpg)

[](https://kids.kiddle.co/Image:Aamir_Khan_at_92.7_BIG_FM_to_promote_Satyamev_Jayate_07.jpg "Enlarge")

 Khan at 92.7 BIG FM radio station.

He continued to act in successful films in the 1990s. These include _[Jo Jeeta Wohi Sikandar](https://kids.kiddle.co/Jo\_Jeeta\_Wohi\_Sikandar "Jo Jeeta Wohi Sikandar")_ (1992) and _Hum Hain Rahi Pyar Ke_ (1993). He also wrote the screenplay for _Hum Hain Rahi Pyar Ke_. _Rangeela_ (1995) was another popular film. _\_[Andaz Apna Apna](https://kids.kiddle.co/Andaz\\_Apna\\_Apna "Andaz Apna Apna")\__ (1994), with [Salman Khan](https://kids.kiddle.co/Salman_Khan "Salman Khan"), became a cult classic over time.

In 1996, his only release was _[Raja Hindustani](https://kids.kiddle.co/Raja\_Hindustani "Raja Hindustani")_, with [Karisma Kapoor](https://kids.kiddle.co/Karisma_Kapoor "Karisma Kapoor"). This film was a huge blockbuster. It earned him his first Filmfare Award for Best Actor. It was also the biggest hit of the year. In 1997, _Ishq_ was another big success. The next year, he starred in _Ghulam_, an action thriller. He also sang a song in the film.

_Sarfarosh_ (1999) was a commercial success. His role in [Deepa Mehta](https://kids.kiddle.co/Deepa_Mehta "Deepa Mehta")'s international film _Earth_ (1998) was also praised. His first film of the 2000s, _Mela_, did not do well.

### Producing, Directing, and Global Success

In 2001, Aamir Khan produced and starred in _Lagaan_. This film was nominated for an [Academy Award for Best Foreign Language Film](https://kids.kiddle.co/Academy_Award_for_Best_International_Feature_Film "Academy Award for Best International Feature Film"). It won many awards in India, and Khan won his second Filmfare Award for Best Actor. After _Lagaan_, he starred in _Dil Chahta Hai_ (2001). He then took a four-year break from acting.

He returned in 2005 with _Mangal Pandey: The Rising_. In 2006, he starred in _Rang De Basanti_. His acting was highly praised, and he won a Filmfare Critics Award for Best Actor. The film was one of the highest-earning films of the year. It was also India's official entry for the Oscars. His next film, _Fanaa_ (2006), saw him play a challenging role.

His 2007 film, _[Taare Zameen Par](https://kids.kiddle.co/Taare\_Zameen\_Par "Taare Zameen Par")_, was his first movie as a director. He also produced it and played a supporting role. The film was very popular with critics and audiences. He won Filmfare Awards for Best Director and Best Film.

In 2008, Khan appeared in _Ghajini_. This film was a huge commercial success. It became the highest-earning Bollywood movie of that year.

[![Image 5: Aamir Khan 2013](https://kids.kiddle.co/images/thumb/b/bd/Aamir_Khan_2013.jpg/170px-Aamir_Khan_2013.jpg)](https://kids.kiddle.co/Image:Aamir_Khan_2013.jpg)

[](https://kids.kiddle.co/Image:Aamir_Khan_2013.jpg "Enlarge")

 Aamir Khan at the trailer launch of _Dhoom 3_ in 2013.

In 2009, he starred in _3 Idiots_. This film became the highest-earning Bollywood film ever at the time. _3 Idiots_ was also very successful in countries like China and [Japan](https://kids.kiddle.co/Japan "Japan"). It helped open up the [Chinese market](https://kids.kiddle.co/Greater_China "Greater China") for Indian films.

His next film was the crime thriller _Talaash: The Answer Lies Within_. He trained for three months to do underwater scenes in the film. _Talaash_ was a "semi-hit" at the box office.

In 2013, he starred in _Dhoom 3_. This film was a massive hit and became the highest-earning Bollywood film of all time. In 2014, he played an alien in _PK_. The film was praised by critics and became the 4th highest-earning Bollywood film ever.

In 2016, he produced and starred in _Dangal_. He played wrestler Mahavir Singh Phogat at different ages. He gained and lost a lot of weight for the role. The film received great reviews and became the highest-earning Bollywood film ever in India. _Dangal_ was also a huge success in China. It became one of the highest-earning non-English language films of all time worldwide. Khan won two more Filmfare Awards for _Dangal_, including his third Best Actor award.

In October 2017, he had a supporting role in his production _Secret Superstar_. This film was very profitable, especially given its small budget. It became one of the highest-earning Indian films of all time.

### Recent Career and Comeback

In November 2018, he starred with [Amitabh Bachchan](https://kids.kiddle.co/Amitabh_Bachchan "Amitabh Bachchan") in _Thugs of Hindostan_. The film received negative reviews and was not a financial success.

In March 2019, Aamir Khan announced his next film, _Laal Singh Chaddha_. This film was an adaptation of _[Forrest Gump](https://kids.kiddle.co/Forrest\_Gump "Forrest Gump")_. It was released on 11 August 2022, marking his return after a four-year break. The film received mixed reviews and did not do well at the box office. Khan expressed sadness about its failure.

After another three-year break, Khan played a basketball coach in _Sitaare Zameen Par_. He helped a team of players with disabilities. The film was a hit and marked his successful comeback.

## Other Important Works

### Film Production and Direction

Aamir Khan co-wrote the screenplay for _Hum Hain Rahi Pyar Ke_, in which he also starred. He started his production company, Aamir Khan Productions, in 1999. _Lagaan_ was its first film. It was India's third film ever to be nominated for an [Academy Award for Best Foreign Language Film](https://kids.kiddle.co/Academy_Award_for_Best_International_Feature_Film "Academy Award for Best International Feature Film"). He also won a National Film Award for producing the documentary _Madness in the Desert_, about the making of _Lagaan_.

In 2007, he directed and produced _[Taare Zameen Par](https://kids.kiddle.co/Taare\_Zameen\_Par "Taare Zameen Par")_. He also played a supporting role. The film was highly praised and successful. It won him the Filmfare Award for Best Director and Best Film. In 2008, his nephew Imran Khan debuted in _Jaane Tu... Ya Jaane Na_, produced by Aamir's company.

Khan also co-wrote the blockbuster film _Ghajini_. He made changes to the original Tamil film and rewrote its ending. In 2010, he released _Peepli Live_, which was India's official entry for the Oscars.

In 2011, he released _Dhobi Ghat_, an art house film directed by his then-wife Kiran Rao. That same year, he co-produced the English language film _Delhi Belly_. This film was praised by critics and was a commercial success. In 2012, he co-produced _Talaash: The Answer Lies Within_.

His production _Secret Superstar_ became one of the most profitable films ever. In China, _Secret Superstar_ broke _Dangal'_ s record for the highest-earning opening weekend for an Indian film. This cemented Khan's status as a superstar in China. _Secret Superstar_ is the third highest-earning Indian film of all time.

Khan co-produced _Laapataa Ladies_, which was released in 2024. It was directed by Kiran Rao and was a satire about women in rural marriages. The film received widespread praise and became very popular on [Netflix](https://kids.kiddle.co/Netflix "Netflix"). It was chosen as the Indian entry for the [Academy Award for Best International Feature Film](https://kids.kiddle.co/Academy_Award_for_Best_International_Feature_Film "Academy Award for Best International Feature Film").

Khan is also producing _Lahore 1947_, which was released in June 2025. It is set during the [1947 Partition of India](https://kids.kiddle.co/Partition_of_India "Partition of India").

### Television Work

Aamir Khan made his TV debut with his talk show, _Satyamev Jayate_, on 6 May 2012. The show discussed important social issues. It was broadcast in eight languages across different channels. The show received positive reviews from social activists and media. Khan was praised for his efforts.

## Aamir Khan in the Media

[![Image 6: Aamir Khan at Satyamev Jayate press conference 13](https://kids.kiddle.co/images/thumb/0/0b/Aamir_Khan_at_Satyamev_Jayate_press_conference_13.jpg/200px-Aamir_Khan_at_Satyamev_Jayate_press_conference_13.jpg)](https://kids.kiddle.co/Image:Aamir_Khan_at_Satyamev_Jayate_press_conference_13.jpg)

[](https://kids.kiddle.co/Image:Aamir_Khan_at_Satyamev_Jayate_press_conference_13.jpg "Enlarge")

 Khan at _Satyamev Jayate_ press conference

Aamir Khan is known for his independent approach to filmmaking. He focuses on the process of making films rather than just the final result. He has a reputation for not attending or accepting popular Indian film awards. He believes that "Indian film awards lack credibility." He only values the [National Film Awards](https://kids.kiddle.co/National_Film_Awards "National Film Awards").

In 2007, he declined an invitation to have a wax statue at [Madame Tussauds](https://kids.kiddle.co/Madame_Tussauds "Madame Tussauds") in London. He said it was not important to him. He has also endorsed several brands over the years.

In April 2013, _Time_ magazine included him in its list of the 100 Most Influential People in the World. He was on the cover of _Time'_ s Asia edition in September 2012. He is very popular in India and also in other countries, especially China. He is the most followed Indian on the Chinese social media site Sina Weibo.

In Chinese media, he is often called a "national treasure of India" or "conscience of India." This is because his films often deal with social issues in India that are also relevant in China. His work is highly respected in China. He is seen as an activist-actor. He has become a household name in China, where he is currently the most famous Indian.

## Humanitarian Causes

[![Image 7: Secretary Clinton and Bollywood Star Aamir Khan](https://kids.kiddle.co/images/thumb/7/7e/Secretary_Clinton_and_Bollywood_Star_Aamir_Khan.jpg/300px-Secretary_Clinton_and_Bollywood_Star_Aamir_Khan.jpg)](https://kids.kiddle.co/Image:Secretary_Clinton_and_Bollywood_Star_Aamir_Khan.jpg)

[](https://kids.kiddle.co/Image:Secretary_Clinton_and_Bollywood_Star_Aamir_Khan.jpg "Enlarge")

 Khan with [United States Secretary of State](https://kids.kiddle.co/United_States_Secretary_of_State "United States Secretary of State")[Hillary Clinton](https://kids.kiddle.co/Hillary_Clinton "Hillary Clinton") in 2009

Aamir Khan has supported many humanitarian causes. In April 2006, he joined protests by the Narmada Bachao Andolan committee. This was after a decision to raise the height of the Narmada dam. He supported the [adivasis](https://kids.kiddle.co/Adivasi "Adivasi") (tribes) who might lose their homes.

He also supported the Janlokpal Bill Movement in August 2011. In July 2012, he met with the prime minister to discuss the issue of manual scavenging in India.

In November 2011, [UNICEF](https://kids.kiddle.co/UNICEF "UNICEF") appointed him as a national brand ambassador. He helped promote child nutrition. He also supports causes like [feminism](https://kids.kiddle.co/Feminism "Feminism") and better [education in India](https://kids.kiddle.co/Education_in_India "Education in India"). These themes are often seen in his films. His success in China has helped improve China–India relations.

In 2016, Aamir Khan worked with the [Maharashtra](https://kids.kiddle.co/Maharashtra "Maharashtra") government to help make the state drought-free. He encouraged people to join him in this effort. He is a co-founder of Paani Foundation with Kiran Rao. This organization works to prevent drought and manage water in Maharashtra.

In October 2014, he was appointed as the UNICEF Goodwill Ambassador for South Asia.

## Personal Life

[![Image 8: Aamir Khan with his wife Kiran Rao at Karan Johar's 40th birthday bash at Taj Lands End (27)](https://kids.kiddle.co/images/thumb/0/01/Aamir_Khan_with_his_wife_Kiran_Rao_at_Karan_Johar%27s_40th_birthday_bash_at_Taj_Lands_End_%2827%29.jpg/150px-Aamir_Khan_with_his_wife_Kiran_Rao_at_Karan_Johar%27s_40th_birthday_bash_at_Taj_Lands_End_%2827%29.jpg)](https://kids.kiddle.co/Image:Aamir_Khan_with_his_wife_Kiran_Rao_at_Karan_Johar%27s_40th_birthday_bash_at_Taj_Lands_End_(27).jpg)

[](https://kids.kiddle.co/Image:Aamir_Khan_with_his_wife_Kiran_Rao_at_Karan_Johar%27s_40th_birthday_bash_at_Taj_Lands_End_(27).jpg "Enlarge")

 Khan with his then wife [Kiran Rao](https://kids.kiddle.co/Kiran_Rao "Kiran Rao") at an event in 2012

Aamir Khan married Reena Dutta on 18 April 1986. They have two children: a son named Junaid and a daughter, Ira. They divorced in December 2002.

On 28 December 2005, he married [Kiran Rao](https://kids.kiddle.co/Kiran_Rao "Kiran Rao"). She was an assistant director on the set of _Lagaan_. On 5 December 2011, they announced the birth of their son, Azad Rao Khan, born through a [surrogate](https://kids.kiddle.co/Surrogacy "Surrogacy") mother. In July 2021, the couple announced their separation. They stated they would raise their son Azad together.

Before becoming a full-time actor, Aamir Khan was a skilled tennis player. He played professionally in state-level championships in the 1980s. In 2014, he played in an exhibition tennis match with famous players like [Roger Federer](https://kids.kiddle.co/Roger_Federer "Roger Federer") and [Novak Djokovic](https://kids.kiddle.co/Novak_Djokovic "Novak Djokovic").

His children have also entered the entertainment industry. In September 2019, his daughter Ira directed a play. His elder son Junaid made his acting debut in the Hindi film _Maharaj_.

On 13 March 2025, Khan publicly introduced Gauri Spratt as his girlfriend at his 60th birthday party.

## Awards and Recognitions

Main article: List of awards and nominations received by Aamir Khan

Aamir Khan has won 9 Filmfare Awards from 32 nominations. These include Best Actor for _Raja Hindustani_ (1996), _Lagaan_ (2001), and _Dangal_ (2016). He also won Best Actor (Critics) for _Rang De Basanti_ (2006). He won Best Film for _Lagaan_, _[Taare Zameen Par](https://kids.kiddle.co/Taare\_Zameen\_Par "Taare Zameen Par")_ (2007), and _Dangal_. He also won Best Director for _Taare Zameen Par_.

He has won four [National Film Awards](https://kids.kiddle.co/National_Film_Awards "National Film Awards"). These include awards for his acting in _Qayamat Se Qayamat Tak_ (1988) and _Raakh_ (1989). He also won as producer of _Lagaan_ and _Madness in the Desert_ (2004). He won as director and producer of _Taare Zameen Par_.

_Lagaan_ was nominated for an [Oscar](https://kids.kiddle.co/Academy_Awards "Academy Awards") for [Academy Award for Best Foreign Language Film](https://kids.kiddle.co/Academy_Award_for_Best_International_Feature_Film "Academy Award for Best International Feature Film") in 2002. _Taare Zameen Par_ and _Peepli Live_ (2010) were also India's submissions to the Oscars. In 2017, _Dangal_ won him the Best Asian Film award at Australia's 7th AACTA Awards. It also won Movie of the Year from China's Douban Film Awards.

Khan has received special honors from the [Government of India](https://kids.kiddle.co/India "India"). These include the [Padma Shri](https://kids.kiddle.co/Padma_Shri "Padma Shri") in 2003 and [Padma Bhushan](https://kids.kiddle.co/Padma_Bhushan "Padma Bhushan") in 2010. He also received an Honorary Doctorate for his contributions to Indian cinema. In 2012, he was on the _Time_ 100 list of most influential people. In 2017, he received an award for "National Treasure of India" from China.

Khan is known for not attending or accepting awards from Indian film ceremonies. This caused some discussion at the 64th National Film Awards in 2017. Despite this, he made an exception for the 2002 Academy Awards for _Lagaan_.

In December 2024, Khan was honored at the opening night of Saudi Arabia's Red Sea Film Festival.

# Reema Lagoo facts for kids

[Kids Encyclopedia Facts](https://kids.kiddle.co/)

| [![Image 3: Reema Lagoo (1 May 2011).jpg](https://kids.kiddle.co/images/thumb/c/c3/Reema_Lagoo_%281_May_2011%29.jpg/300px-Reema_Lagoo_%281_May_2011%29.jpg)](https://kids.kiddle.co/Image:Reema_Lagoo_(1_May_2011).jpg) Lagoo in May 2011 |

**Reema Lagoo** (born **Nayan Bhadbhade**; 21 June 1958 – 18 May 2017) was a famous Indian actress. She worked in both Hindi and Marathi films, as well as on television and in theatre. She became very well-known for playing motherly roles in many popular movies and TV shows during the 1990s and early 2000s.

She was loved by many for her warm and kind portrayals of mothers. Some of her most famous TV shows were _Shriman Shrimati_ and _Tu Tu Main Main_.

## Contents

*   [Reema Lagoo's Acting Journey](https://kids.kiddle.co/Reema_Lagoo#Reema_Lagoo.27s_Acting_Journey)

## Reema Lagoo's Acting Journey

[![Image 4: Rohini Hattangadi and Reema Lagoo](https://kids.kiddle.co/images/thumb/1/1c/Rohini_Hattangadi_and_Reema_Lagoo.jpg/300px-Rohini_Hattangadi_and_Reema_Lagoo.jpg)](https://kids.kiddle.co/Image:Rohini_Hattangadi_and_Reema_Lagoo.jpg)

[](https://kids.kiddle.co/Image:Rohini_Hattangadi_and_Reema_Lagoo.jpg "Enlarge")

 Lagoo with fellow actress Rohini Hattangadi.

Reema Lagoo started acting when she was a child. Her mother was also an actress in Marathi theatre and films, which inspired her. After a break, she returned to acting as an adult in Marathi plays in Mumbai.

She became more widely recognized through her roles in television shows and films. Her first film was the Marathi movie _Sinhasan_ in 1979.

### Hindi Films

Reema Lagoo often played supporting roles in Hindi films, especially as the mother of the main characters. She became famous after appearing in _[Qayamat Se Qayamat Tak](https://kids.kiddle.co/Qayamat\_Se\_Qayamat\_Tak "Qayamat Se Qayamat Tak")_ (1988), where she played [Juhi Chawla](https://kids.kiddle.co/Juhi_Chawla "Juhi Chawla")'s mother.

She then starred in the very successful film _Maine Pyar Kiya_ (1989) as [Salman Khan](https://kids.kiddle.co/Salman_Khan "Salman Khan")'s mother. She also appeared in other popular movies like _Saajan_ (1991), _Gumrah_ (1993), _Jai Kishen_ (1994), and _Rangeela_ (1995).

Some of her biggest hit films include _Hum Aapke Hain Koun..!_ (1994), _Yeh Dillagi_ (1994), _Dilwale_ (1994), _[Kuch Kuch Hota Hai](https://kids.kiddle.co/Kuch\_Kuch\_Hota\_Hai "Kuch Kuch Hota Hai")_ (1998), _Kal Ho Naa Ho_ (2003), _Hum Saath-Saath Hain_ (1999), and _Vaastav: The Reality_ (1999). In _Vaastav_, she played the mother of a gangster, a role that won her an award. People in the media often called her a "new-age mother" in Hindi cinema because of her modern and strong portrayals.

Even though she was known for playing mothers, she also took on different kinds of roles. For example, she played a dancer in _Aakrosh_ (1980) and a tough businesswoman in _Yeh Dillagi_ (1994).

### Marathi Films

Reema Lagoo also had a significant career in Marathi films. She won the Maharashtra State Film Award for Best Actress for her role in the 2002 film _Reshamgaath_. Her performance in _Janma_ (2011) was also highly praised. She received the V Shantaram Award from the Government of Maharashtra for her contributions to Marathi cinema.

### Television Shows

Reema Lagoo was also a successful television actress in both Hindi and Marathi languages. She started her TV career in 1985 with the Hindi series _Khandaan_.

Her roles as Kokila Kulkarni in _Shriman Shrimati_ and as Devaki Verma in _Tu Tu Main Main_ were her most popular TV appearances. For _Tu Tu Main Main_, she even won an award for Best Actress in a Comic Role. She also appeared on the Marathi show _Maanacha Muzra_, which celebrates famous Marathi personalities.

## Personal Life

Reema Lagoo was born on June 21, 1958, with the name Nayan Bhadbhade. Her mother, Mandakini Bhadbhade, was a well-known Marathi stage actress. Reema's talent for acting was noticed when she was a student in Pune.

After finishing school, she started acting professionally. For ten years, starting in 1979, she worked at the Union Bank of India in Mumbai. During this time, she also continued to act in television and films.

She met Vivek Lagoo, who was also an actor and worked at the same bank, in 1976. They got married in 1978, and she took the name Reema Lagoo. They later separated, but they remained friends. Their daughter, Mrunmayee, is also an actress and a theatre director.

## Passing Away

Reema Lagoo was filming for the TV series _Naamkarann_ until the evening of May 17, 2017. Later that night, she felt chest pain and was taken to a hospital in Mumbai. She sadly passed away at 3:15 AM on May 18, 2017, due to a [cardiac arrest](https://kids.kiddle.co/Cardiac_arrest "Cardiac arrest") (a sudden stop of the heart). At the time, she was described as being in good health. Her funeral was held in Mumbai by her daughter.

# Rajput facts for kids

[Kids Encyclopedia Facts](https://kids.kiddle.co/)

| Quick facts for kids Rajput |
| --- |
| [![Image 3: Rajpoots 2.png](https://kids.kiddle.co/images/thumb/1/16/Rajpoots_2.png/250px-Rajpoots_2.png)](https://kids.kiddle.co/Image:Rajpoots_2.png) An 1876 engraving of the Rajputs of **Rajputana**, from the _Illustrated London News_ |
| Religions | [Hinduism](https://kids.kiddle.co/Hinduism "Hinduism") and [Islam](https://kids.kiddle.co/Islam "Islam") |
| Languages | [Hindi](https://kids.kiddle.co/Hindi "Hindi"), Haryanvi, [Punjabi](https://kids.kiddle.co/Punjabi_language "Punjabi language"), [Bhojpuri](https://kids.kiddle.co/Bhojpuri_language "Bhojpuri language"), [Urdu](https://kids.kiddle.co/Urdu "Urdu"), [Gujarati](https://kids.kiddle.co/Gujarati_language "Gujarati language"), [Maithili](https://kids.kiddle.co/Maithili_language "Maithili language"), Marwari, Mewari, [Sindhi](https://kids.kiddle.co/Sindhi_language "Sindhi language"), [Dogri](https://kids.kiddle.co/Dogri_language "Dogri language") and Pahari |
| Region | [Uttar Pradesh](https://kids.kiddle.co/Uttar_Pradesh "Uttar Pradesh"), [Punjab](https://kids.kiddle.co/Punjab "Punjab"), [Rajasthan](https://kids.kiddle.co/Rajasthan "Rajasthan"), [Gujarat](https://kids.kiddle.co/Gujarat "Gujarat"), [Himachal Pradesh](https://kids.kiddle.co/Himachal_Pradesh "Himachal Pradesh"), [Uttarakhand](https://kids.kiddle.co/Uttarakhand "Uttarakhand"), [Haryana](https://kids.kiddle.co/Haryana "Haryana"), [Jammu and Kashmir](https://kids.kiddle.co/Jammu_and_Kashmir "Jammu and Kashmir"), [Azad Kashmir](https://kids.kiddle.co/Azad_Kashmir "Azad Kashmir"), [Bihar](https://kids.kiddle.co/Bihar "Bihar"), [Jharkhand](https://kids.kiddle.co/Jharkhand "Jharkhand"), [Madhya Pradesh](https://kids.kiddle.co/Madhya_Pradesh "Madhya Pradesh"), [Maharashtra](https://kids.kiddle.co/Maharashtra "Maharashtra"), and [Sindh](https://kids.kiddle.co/Sindh "Sindh") |

The **Rajputs** are an important group of people from [India](https://kids.kiddle.co/India "India"). They are mostly [Hindu](https://kids.kiddle.co/Hinduism "Hinduism") and are known for being brave warriors. For a long time, they ruled many kingdoms across India. The word "Rajput" comes from the Sanskrit words "Raja-putra," which means "son of a king."

Rajputs believe they are descendants of ancient royal families. They were part of the [Kshatriya](https://kids.kiddle.co/Kshatriya "Kshatriya") class, which was traditionally the warrior and ruler class in ancient Indian society. Their history is full of stories about courage, honor, and loyalty.

## Contents

*   [Where Do Rajputs Live?](https://kids.kiddle.co/Rajput#Where_Do_Rajputs_Live.3F)
*   [What Are the Rajput Clans?](https://kids.kiddle.co/Rajput#What_Are_the_Rajput_Clans.3F)

*   [Images for kids](https://kids.kiddle.co/Rajput#Images_for_kids)
*   [See also](https://kids.kiddle.co/Rajput#See_also)

## Where Do Rajputs Live?

Rajputs live in many parts of India and nearby regions. You can find them in states like [Rajasthan](https://kids.kiddle.co/Rajasthan "Rajasthan"), [Uttar Pradesh](https://kids.kiddle.co/Uttar_Pradesh "Uttar Pradesh"), [Punjab](https://kids.kiddle.co/Punjab "Punjab"), and [Gujarat](https://kids.kiddle.co/Gujarat "Gujarat"). They also live in parts of [Pakistan](https://kids.kiddle.co/Pakistan "Pakistan") and [Nepal](https://kids.kiddle.co/Nepal "Nepal"). Over centuries, they spread across different areas, bringing their culture and traditions with them.

## What Are the Rajput Clans?

The Rajputs are made up of 36 different groups, called clans. These clans are divided into three main lines, or "vanshas," based on their legendary origins:

*   **Suryavanshi:** These Rajputs believe they are descendants of the sun god, [Surya](https://kids.kiddle.co/Surya "Surya").
*   **Chandravanshi:** These Rajputs believe their ancestors came from the moon god, [Chandra](https://kids.kiddle.co/Chandra "Chandra").
*   **Agnivanshi:** These Rajputs believe they came from the fire god, [Agni](https://kids.kiddle.co/Agni "Agni").

Each clan has its own unique history and traditions, but they all share the common Rajput identity.

## Rajput History and Culture

Rajputs were famous for building strong forts and beautiful palaces. These buildings often show amazing art and architecture. They were also known for their bravery in battles. Many Rajput rulers defended their kingdoms with great courage.

Their culture is rich with traditions, music, and dance. Stories of their heroes and queens are still told today. Honor and pride are very important values in Rajput culture.

# Dev Anand facts for kids

[Kids Encyclopedia Facts](https://kids.kiddle.co/)

| Quick facts for kids Dev Anand |
| --- |
| [![Image 3: Dev Anand in Kashti.jpg](https://kids.kiddle.co/images/thumb/3/3f/Dev_Anand_in_Kashti.jpg/300px-Dev_Anand_in_Kashti.jpg)](https://kids.kiddle.co/Image:Dev_Anand_in_Kashti.jpg) Dev Anand, c. 1954 |
| Born | Dharamdev Pishorimal Anand (1923-09-26)26 September 1923 [Shakargarh](https://kids.kiddle.co/Shakargarh_Tehsil "Shakargarh Tehsil"), Punjab, [British India](https://kids.kiddle.co/British_Raj "British Raj") (present-day [Punjab](https://kids.kiddle.co/Punjab_(Pakistan) "Punjab (Pakistan)"), [Pakistan](https://kids.kiddle.co/Pakistan "Pakistan")) |
| Died | 3 December 2011(2011-12-03) (aged 88) [London](https://kids.kiddle.co/London "London"), [England](https://kids.kiddle.co/England "England") |
| Other names | Dev Sahab, Evergreen star |
| Alma mater | Government College, Lahore ([BA](https://kids.kiddle.co/Bachelor_of_Arts "Bachelor of Arts")) |
| Occupation | * Actor * producer * director |
| Years active | 1946–2011 |
| Spouse(s) | Kalpana Kartik ​ (m.1954)​ |
| Children | 2; including Suneil Anand |
| Relatives | See Anand-Sahni family |
| Awards | * [Padma Bhushan](https://kids.kiddle.co/Padma_Bhushan "Padma Bhushan") (2001) * [Dadasaheb Phalke Award](https://kids.kiddle.co/Dadasaheb_Phalke_Award "Dadasaheb Phalke Award") (2002) |
| Signature |
| [![Image 4: Dev Anand signature.svg](https://kids.kiddle.co/images/thumb/7/7c/Dev_Anand_signature.svg/150px-Dev_Anand_signature.svg.png)](https://kids.kiddle.co/Image:Dev_Anand_signature.svg) |

**Dharamdev Pishorimal Anand** (born 26 September 1923 – died 3 December 2011), known as **Dev Anand**, was a famous Indian actor, writer, director, and producer. He worked in Hindi cinema for over sixty years. He was one of the most successful actors in [Indian cinema](https://kids.kiddle.co/Indian_cinema "Indian cinema"). People often called him part of the "Trinity – The Golden Trio" along with [Raj Kapoor](https://kids.kiddle.co/Raj_Kapoor "Raj Kapoor") and [Dilip Kumar](https://kids.kiddle.co/Dilip_Kumar "Dilip Kumar"), who were also very popular actors of his time.

The Government of India honored him with the [Padma Bhushan](https://kids.kiddle.co/Padma_Bhushan "Padma Bhushan") award in 2001 and the [Dadasaheb Phalke Award](https://kids.kiddle.co/Dadasaheb_Phalke_Award "Dadasaheb Phalke Award") in 2002. These are two of India's highest honors for people who have contributed a lot to Indian cinema. He also won the Filmfare Award for Best Actor twice and a special Filmfare Lifetime Achievement Award in 1993 for his amazing career.

Dev Anand's films often explored his views on the world and talked about important social topics. He had a unique acting style that many other actors tried to copy.

## Contents

*   [Early Life and Education](https://kids.kiddle.co/Dev_Anand#Early_Life_and_Education)
*   [Career Beginnings](https://kids.kiddle.co/Dev_Anand#Career_Beginnings)
    *   [Early Success and Film Partnerships](https://kids.kiddle.co/Dev_Anand#Early_Success_and_Film_Partnerships)
    *   [Romantic Hero and Director in the 1960s and 1970s](https://kids.kiddle.co/Dev_Anand#Romantic_Hero_and_Director_in_the_1960s_and_1970s)
    *   [Political Involvement and Later Career](https://kids.kiddle.co/Dev_Anand#Political_Involvement_and_Later_Career)

*   [Recognition and Legacy](https://kids.kiddle.co/Dev_Anand#Recognition_and_Legacy)
*   [Personal Life](https://kids.kiddle.co/Dev_Anand#Personal_Life)
*   [Death](https://kids.kiddle.co/Dev_Anand#Death)
*   [Awards and Honours](https://kids.kiddle.co/Dev_Anand#Awards_and_Honours)
    *   [Major Awards](https://kids.kiddle.co/Dev_Anand#Major_Awards)
    *   [Other Honours](https://kids.kiddle.co/Dev_Anand#Other_Honours)

*   [Selected Filmography](https://kids.kiddle.co/Dev_Anand#Selected_Filmography)
*   [Images for kids](https://kids.kiddle.co/Dev_Anand#Images_for_kids)
*   [See also](https://kids.kiddle.co/Dev_Anand#See_also)

## Early Life and Education

Dev Anand was born Dharamdev Pishorimal Anand on 26 September 1923. His birthplace was in a region called Shakargarh, which was then part of British India (now in Pakistan). His father was a lawyer. Dev was one of four sons. His older brothers were Manmohan Anand and [Chetan Anand](https://kids.kiddle.co/Chetan_Anand_(director) "Chetan Anand (director)"), and his younger brother was [Vijay Anand](https://kids.kiddle.co/Vijay_Anand_(filmmaker) "Vijay Anand (filmmaker)"). His sister, Sheel Kanta Kapur, is the mother of film director [Shekhar Kapur](https://kids.kiddle.co/Shekhar_Kapur "Shekhar Kapur").

Dev Anand went to school in Dalhousie and Dharamshala. He later earned a Bachelor of Arts (BA) degree in English Literature from the Government College, Lahore in British India. In 1949, he and his elder brother Chetan Anand started their own film company called Navketan Films.

## Career Beginnings

[![Image 5: Dev Anand 2013 stamp of India](https://kids.kiddle.co/images/thumb/a/af/Dev_Anand_2013_stamp_of_India.jpg/330px-Dev_Anand_2013_stamp_of_India.jpg)](https://kids.kiddle.co/Image:Dev_Anand_2013_stamp_of_India.jpg)

[](https://kids.kiddle.co/Image:Dev_Anand_2013_stamp_of_India.jpg "Enlarge")

 Dev Anand on a 2013 stamp of India

After finishing his degree, Dev Anand moved to Bombay (now Mumbai) in the early 1940s. He started his career working in a military office and then as a clerk. However, he really wanted to become an actor. He was inspired by famous actors like [Ashok Kumar](https://kids.kiddle.co/Ashok_Kumar "Ashok Kumar").

Dev Anand got his first big acting role in the film _Hum Ek Hain_ (1946). This movie was about Hindu-Muslim unity. While filming, he became good friends with another actor, [Guru Dutt](https://kids.kiddle.co/Guru_Dutt "Guru Dutt"). They made a promise: if one of them became successful, they would help the other. This promise led to many great films later on.

### Early Success and Film Partnerships

In the late 1940s, Dev Anand starred in several films with the singer-actress [Suraiya](https://kids.kiddle.co/Suraiya "Suraiya"). They made seven successful movies together, including _Vidya_ (1948) and _Jeet_ (1949). Suraiya was a bigger star at the time. Their partnership was very popular, but Suraiya's family did not approve of their close friendship, so they stopped working together.

In 1948, Dev Anand got another big break from actor [Ashok Kumar](https://kids.kiddle.co/Ashok_Kumar "Ashok Kumar"), who chose him for the film _Ziddi_. This movie was a huge hit. After its success, Dev Anand decided to start producing his own films. In 1949, he launched his company, Navketan Films, which has produced many movies over the years.

Dev Anand chose his friend [Guru Dutt](https://kids.kiddle.co/Guru_Dutt "Guru Dutt") to direct his crime thriller film, _Baazi_ (1951). This film was a big success and helped create a new style of urban crime movies in Bollywood. In _Baazi_, Dev Anand starred with Kalpana Kartik, who later became his wife. They made several successful films together, like _Taxi Driver_ (1954). They got married in 1954 and had two children, Suneil and Devina. After marriage, Kalpana Kartik stopped acting.

Dev Anand became known for his fast way of delivering dialogues and nodding his head while speaking. This style became his trademark in films like _Jaal_ (1952) and _C.I.D._ (1956). His films in the 1950s were often mysteries, romantic comedies, or movies with important social messages. He won his first Filmfare Award for Best Actor for the film _Kala Pani_ (1958).

### Romantic Hero and Director in the 1960s and 1970s

In the 1960s, Dev Anand became known as a romantic hero. He starred in popular films like _Manzil_ and _Tere Ghar Ke Samne_ with [Nutan](https://kids.kiddle.co/Nutan "Nutan"), and _Jab Pyar Kisi Se Hota Hai_. One of his most famous films from this period was _Hum Dono_ (1961), where he played a double role. This film was also a big hit.

His first color film was _Guide_ (1965), starring [Waheeda Rehman](https://kids.kiddle.co/Waheeda_Rehman "Waheeda Rehman"). This movie was based on a famous novel by [R. K. Narayan](https://kids.kiddle.co/R._K._Narayan "R. K. Narayan"). Dev Anand himself helped make the film happen. _Guide_, directed by his younger brother Vijay Anand, was highly praised and was even considered for an [Academy Award for Best Foreign Language Film](https://kids.kiddle.co/Academy_Award_for_Best_International_Feature_Film "Academy Award for Best International Feature Film"). Dev Anand gave a powerful performance as Raju, a guide who helps a woman find her freedom.

He worked with his brother Vijay Anand again on the successful thriller _Jewel Thief_ (1967) and _Johny Mera Naam_ (1970), which was a huge hit and helped make [Hema Malini](https://kids.kiddle.co/Hema_Malini "Hema Malini") a big star.

In the 1970s, Dev Anand started directing films. His first movie as a director, _Prem Pujari_, was not a big success at first but later became a favorite for many. He found success with his 1971 film _Hare Rama Hare Krishna_, which talked about the hippie culture. This film introduced Zeenat Aman, who became very famous overnight. Dev Anand also starred in _Tere Mere Sapne_ (1971), which was also a success.

Even as he got older, Dev Anand continued to star in many successful films in the 1970s, like _Banarasi Babu_ (1973), _Heera Panna_ (1973), and _Warrant_ (1975). He was known as the "Evergreen Star" because he continued to act with young heroines and make popular movies even in his fifties. His film _Des Pardes_ (1978) was a big hit and introduced actress Tina Munim.

### Political Involvement and Later Career

Dev Anand was also involved in politics. He spoke out against the "Emergency" period in India in the late 1970s, which was a time when the government had special powers. He even started a political party called the "National Party of India," but he later closed it down.

His success continued into the 1980s with films like _Lootmaar_ and _Swami Dada_ (1982). He tried to launch his son, Suneil Anand, as an actor in the film _Anand Aur Anand_ (1984), but the movie was not successful.

Despite this, Dev Anand continued to act and direct. His films _Hum Naujawan_ (1985) and _Lashkar_ (1989) were successful. He even acted with younger stars like [Aamir Khan](https://kids.kiddle.co/Aamir_Khan "Aamir Khan") in _Awwal Number_ (1990). His last film, _Chargesheet_, was released in 2011, shortly before his death.

Dev Anand appeared in 114 Hindi films and two English films, including the English version of _Guide_. He holds the record for the second most solo lead roles in Hindi films, with 92.

## Recognition and Legacy

[![Image 6: Raj Kapoor, Dilip Kumar and Dev Anand with Prime Minister Jawaharlal Nehru](https://kids.kiddle.co/images/thumb/d/db/Raj_Kapoor%2C_Dilip_Kumar_and_Dev_Anand_with_Prime_Minister_Jawaharlal_Nehru.jpg/330px-Raj_Kapoor%2C_Dilip_Kumar_and_Dev_Anand_with_Prime_Minister_Jawaharlal_Nehru.jpg)](https://kids.kiddle.co/Image:Raj_Kapoor,_Dilip_Kumar_and_Dev_Anand_with_Prime_Minister_Jawaharlal_Nehru.jpg)

[](https://kids.kiddle.co/Image:Raj_Kapoor,_Dilip_Kumar_and_Dev_Anand_with_Prime_Minister_Jawaharlal_Nehru.jpg "Enlarge")

 Dev Anand with [Prime Minister Nehru](https://kids.kiddle.co/Jawaharlal_Nehru "Jawaharlal Nehru") (second from left) and fellow actors [Dilip Kumar](https://kids.kiddle.co/Dilip_Kumar "Dilip Kumar") (extreme left) and [Raj Kapoor](https://kids.kiddle.co/Raj_Kapoor "Raj Kapoor") (extreme right) (c. 1950s).

Dev Anand was often compared to the famous Hollywood actor [Gregory Peck](https://kids.kiddle.co/Gregory_Peck "Gregory Peck"). However, Dev Anand always said he wanted to be known as himself, Dev Anand, not as someone else. He met Gregory Peck several times and they had friendly conversations.

Dev Anand directed 19 films and produced 35 films. Many of his films were successful. He also wrote stories for 13 of his movies. Critics often said his films were ahead of their time. His movies are also famous for their wonderful songs. He worked closely with many great music composers and singers, like [Sachin Dev Burman](https://kids.kiddle.co/S._D._Burman "S. D. Burman"), [Rahul Dev Burman](https://kids.kiddle.co/R._D._Burman "R. D. Burman"), and [Kishore Kumar](https://kids.kiddle.co/Kishore_Kumar "Kishore Kumar"), to create memorable music.

In 2007, Dev Anand released his autobiography (a book about his own life) called _Romancing with Life_. In 2011, his 1961 film _Hum Dono_ was made into a color film and re-released.

Dev Anand is also known for discovering and helping many new talents in the film industry. He gave actors like [Jackie Shroff](https://kids.kiddle.co/Jackie_Shroff "Jackie Shroff"), Tabu, Zeenat Aman, and Tina Munim their first big breaks. He also encouraged music composers like [Rajesh Roshan](https://kids.kiddle.co/Rajesh_Roshan "Rajesh Roshan"). Many famous people in Indian cinema, like [Guru Dutt](https://kids.kiddle.co/Guru_Dutt "Guru Dutt"), [Waheeda Rehman](https://kids.kiddle.co/Waheeda_Rehman "Waheeda Rehman"), and [Shekhar Kapur](https://kids.kiddle.co/Shekhar_Kapur "Shekhar Kapur"), started their careers under Dev Anand's film company, Navketan Films.

## Personal Life

Dev Anand married Kalpana Kartik (whose real name was Mona Singha) in 1954. She was also a Bollywood actress. They had a quiet wedding during the filming of their movie _Taxi Driver_. They had a son named Suneil and a daughter named Devina.

## Death

Dev Anand passed away in London on 3 December 2011, at the age of 88, due to a heart attack. His death happened just two months after his last film, _Chargesheet_, was released. His funeral service was held in London, and his ashes were later brought back to India to be immersed in the Godavari River.

## Awards and Honours

[![Image 7: Dev Anand at the 50th National Film Award function in New Delhi](https://kids.kiddle.co/images/thumb/6/68/Dev_Anand_at_the_50th_National_Film_Award_function_in_New_Delhi.jpg/300px-Dev_Anand_at_the_50th_National_Film_Award_function_in_New_Delhi.jpg)](https://kids.kiddle.co/Image:Dev_Anand_at_the_50th_National_Film_Award_function_in_New_Delhi.jpg)

[](https://kids.kiddle.co/Image:Dev_Anand_at_the_50th_National_Film_Award_function_in_New_Delhi.jpg "Enlarge")

 Dev Anand at the 50th National Film Award function in New Delhi when he was awarded [Dadasaheb Phalke Award](https://kids.kiddle.co/Dadasaheb_Phalke_Award "Dadasaheb Phalke Award"), 2003

The Government of India honored Dev Anand with the [Padma Bhushan](https://kids.kiddle.co/Padma_Bhushan "Padma Bhushan") in 2001 and the [Dadasaheb Phalke Award](https://kids.kiddle.co/Dadasaheb_Phalke_Award "Dadasaheb Phalke Award") in 2002. These are very high awards for his contributions to Indian cinema. He won the Filmfare Award for Best Actor for his roles in _Kala Pani_ and _Guide_.

### Major Awards

*   2001 – [Padma Bhushan](https://kids.kiddle.co/Padma_Bhushan "Padma Bhushan") (India's third highest civilian award)
*   1965 – National Film Award for Best Feature Film in Hindi for _Guide_
*   2002 – [Dadasaheb Phalke Award](https://kids.kiddle.co/Dadasaheb_Phalke_Award "Dadasaheb Phalke Award") (India's highest award for cinema)
*   1959 – Best Actor for _Kala Pani_
*   1967 – Best Actor for _Guide_
*   1967 – Best Film for _Guide_
*   1993 – Lifetime Achievement Award

### Other Honours

Dev Anand received many other awards and honors throughout his career, including:

*   1995 – Screen Lifetime Achievement Award
*   2000 – "Star of the Millennium" Award in Silicon Valley, California.
*   2001 – "Evergreen Star of the Millennium" Award at the Zee Gold Bollywood Awards.
*   2003 – Lifetime Achievement Award at the IIFA Award in South Africa.
*   2007 – Punjab Ratan Award for his contributions to art and entertainment.
*   2013 – A brass statue of Dev Anand was unveiled at the Walk of the Stars in Mumbai.
*   2013 – A postage stamp with his picture was released by India Post to honor him.

**Chetan Anand** (born January 3, 1921 – died July 6, 1997) was a famous [Hindi](https://kids.kiddle.co/Bollywood "Bollywood") film producer, writer, and director from India. His first movie, _Neecha Nagar_, won a big award called the Grand Prix Prize (now the Golden Palm) at the very first [Cannes Film Festival](https://kids.kiddle.co/Cannes_Film_Festival "Cannes Film Festival") in 1946. Later, in 1949, he helped start a film company called Navketan Films with his younger brother, [Dev Anand](https://kids.kiddle.co/Dev_Anand "Dev Anand").

## About Chetan Anand's Life

### Early Years and Education

Chetan Anand was born on January 3, 1921, in [Lahore](https://kids.kiddle.co/Lahore "Lahore"), which was part of [British India](https://kids.kiddle.co/British_India "British India") at the time. His father, Pishori Lal Anand, was a successful lawyer.

Chetan studied Hindu scriptures at Gurukul Kangri Vishwavidyalaya. He later earned a degree in English from [Government College Lahore](https://kids.kiddle.co/Government_College_University "Government College University"). In the 1930s, he was part of the [Indian National Congress](https://kids.kiddle.co/Indian_National_Congress "Indian National Congress"). He also worked for the [BBC](https://kids.kiddle.co/BBC "BBC") and taught at [The Doon School](https://kids.kiddle.co/The_Doon_School "The Doon School") in [Dehradun](https://kids.kiddle.co/Dehradun "Dehradun") for a while.

### Starting a Film Career

In the early 1940s, Chetan Anand taught history. He wrote a film script about the ancient king [Ashoka the Great](https://kids.kiddle.co/Ashoka_the_Great "Ashoka the Great"). He took his script to director Phani Majumdar in [Bombay](https://kids.kiddle.co/Mumbai "Mumbai").

Chetan also tried to join the Indian Civil Service (ICS) in [London](https://kids.kiddle.co/London "London") but did not pass the exams. Luckily, Phani Majumdar chose him to act as the main character in his Hindi film, _Rajkumar_, which came out in 1944. Chetan also joined the Indian People's Theatre Association (IPTA) in Bombay.

### Directing Award-Winning Films

Chetan Anand soon became a film director. His movie _Neecha Nagar_ was highly praised. It won the [Palme d'Or](https://kids.kiddle.co/Palme_d%27Or "Palme d'Or") (Best Film) award at the [Cannes Film Festival](https://kids.kiddle.co/Cannes_Film_Festival "Cannes Film Festival") in 1946. This was the first film for actress Kamini Kaushal. It was also the first Indian film to get international recognition. The famous musician [Pandit Ravi Shankar](https://kids.kiddle.co/Ravi_Shankar "Ravi Shankar") also made his debut in this film.

By the early 1950s, Chetan and his younger brother [Dev Anand](https://kids.kiddle.co/Dev_Anand "Dev Anand") started their own film company, Navketan Productions, in Bombay. Their first film was _Afsar_, starring Dev Anand and [Suraiya](https://kids.kiddle.co/Suraiya "Suraiya"). It was a moderate success. Chetan also directed _Taxi Driver_ and _Aandhiyan_ for Navketan.

### Acting and New Productions

While directing, Chetan Anand also acted in movies sometimes. He appeared in _Humsafar_ in 1957. In the same year, he directed and acted in two movies, _Arpan_ and _Anjali_. He also acted in films like _Kala Bazar_, _Kinare-Kinare_, and _Hindustan Ki Kasam_, which he also directed.

Later, Chetan Anand started his own production company called Himalaya films. He worked with talented people like photographer Jal Mistry, music director Madan Mohan, writer [Kaifi Azmi](https://kids.kiddle.co/Kaifi_Azmi "Kaifi Azmi"), and actress Priya Rajvansh. Together, they created memorable films such as _Haqeeqat_, _Heer Raanjha_, _Hanste Zakhm_, and _Hindustan Ki Kasam_.

Chetan Anand is known for discovering the famous actor [Rajesh Khanna](https://kids.kiddle.co/Rajesh_Khanna "Rajesh Khanna"). He cast Khanna in his first film, _Aakhri Khat_. This movie is remembered for its beautiful locations, songs, and the child star 'Bunty'. Chetan later directed Rajesh Khanna again in the film _Kudrat_, which was about reincarnation.

Besides his 17 feature films, Chetan Anand also created a well-known television series. This was _Param Vir Chakra_, which was shown on Doordarshan in 1988.

### Family Life

In 1943, Chetan Anand married Uma Chatterji. They had two sons, Ketan Anand and Vivek Anand. After some years, Chetan and Uma separated.

Many years later, Chetan Anand formed a close partnership with Priya Rajvansh. She was the lead actress in his film _Haqeeqat_. Their relationship lasted for the rest of their lives. Priya Rajvansh acted in every film Chetan Anand made after _Haqeeqat_. She did not work in any other films.

Chetan Anand passed away on July 6, 1997, in [Mumbai](https://kids.kiddle.co/Mumbai "Mumbai"), at the age of 76. He left a part of his wealth to Priya Rajvansh. This included the right for her to live in his large beachfront house in Juhu, [Mumbai](https://kids.kiddle.co/Mumbai "Mumbai"), for her entire life. This arrangement ensured she could live in the home they shared, while the property would go to his sons after her passing.

## Chetan Anand's Legacy

_Chetan Anand: The Poetics of Film_ is a book about him. It was written by his wife Uma Anand and son Ketan Anand. The book was released in 2006. A documentary with the same name, made by Ketan Anand, came out in 2008.

A special showing of his films was held at the Stuttgart Film Festival. Another one took place at the India International Centre in [New Delhi](https://kids.kiddle.co/New_Delhi "New Delhi") in 2007.

**Kulbhushan Kharbanda** is a famous [Indian](https://kids.kiddle.co/India "India") actor. He was born on October 21, 1944. He has acted in many [Hindi](https://kids.kiddle.co/Hindi "Hindi") and [Punjabi](https://kids.kiddle.co/Punjabi_language "Punjabi language") films. People often remember him for playing the bad guy, Shakaal, in the movie _Shaan_ (1980).

Kulbhushan Kharbanda started his acting journey in theatre groups in the 1960s. He then moved into films in 1974. He worked in special "parallel cinema" films before becoming popular in mainstream Hindi movies. He appeared in well-known films like _Arth_ (1982) and _Ek Chadar Maili Si_ (1986). He also starred in all three parts of [Deepa Mehta](https://kids.kiddle.co/Deepa_Mehta "Deepa Mehta")'s famous "Elements trilogy": _Fire_ (1996), _Earth_ (1998), and _Water_ (2005).

## Kulbhushan Kharbanda's Acting Journey

Kulbhushan Kharbanda began his career in theatre. After finishing his studies, he and his friends started a theatre group called "Abhiyaan." Later, he joined "Yatrik," a theatre group in Delhi. He was the first paid actor there.

In 1972, he moved to [Kolkata](https://kids.kiddle.co/Kolkata "Kolkata") and worked with another theatre group called "Padatik." This group performed plays in Hindi. After some time, he moved to Mumbai to start acting in films.

### Early Films and Big Break

Kulbhushan Kharbanda first gained attention in the film _Nishaant_ (1974). This movie was directed by [Shyam Benegal](https://kids.kiddle.co/Shyam_Benegal "Shyam Benegal"). He worked with Shyam Benegal on many other films, including _Manthan_ (1976) and _Junoon_ (1978). He became a regular actor for directors who made "parallel cinema" films. These films were often more artistic and realistic.

His role as the bald villain Shakaal in _Shaan_ (1980) made him very famous. This movie helped him move into mainstream cinema, which means more popular and widely seen films.

### Popular Roles and Movies

After _Shaan_, Kulbhushan Kharbanda appeared in many big movies. Some of these include _Shakti_ (1982), _Ghayal_ (1990), and _[Jo Jeeta Wohi Sikandar](https://kids.kiddle.co/Jo\_Jeeta\_Wohi\_Sikandar "Jo Jeeta Wohi Sikandar")_ (1992). He also acted in _Gupt_ (1997) and _Border_ (1997).

Even while doing mainstream films, he continued to act in art films. These included _Chakra_ (1981), _Arth_ (1982), and _Monsoon Wedding_ (2001). He also played important roles in historical films like _[Jodha Akbar](https://kids.kiddle.co/Jodha\_Akbar "Jodha Akbar")_ and _Lagaan_.

Kulbhushan Kharbanda has also acted in several Punjabi films. He was the hero in the well-known film _Chan Pardesi_ (1980). He also starred in the Punjabi comedy _Mahaul Theek Hai_ (1999).

He has worked with director [Deepa Mehta](https://kids.kiddle.co/Deepa_Mehta "Deepa Mehta") on six movies, including her famous trilogy: _Earth_, _Fire_, and _Water_. He even acted in a [German](https://kids.kiddle.co/Germany "Germany") film in 2009.

### Television and Stage Work

Besides films, Kulbhushan Kharbanda has appeared in TV shows. Some of these include _Shanno Ki Shaadi_ and _Mahi Ve_. He has also continued to perform in plays on stage. His recent stage work includes the play _Atmakatha_.

## Films and TV Shows
