**Sidney Edmond Jocelyn Ackland** (29 February 1928 – 19 November 2023) was an English actor who appeared in more than 130 film, radio and television roles.[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Joss_Ackland#cite_note-1) He was nominated for the [BAFTA Award for Best Actor in a Supporting Role](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/BAFTA_Award_for_Best_Actor_in_a_Supporting_Role "BAFTA Award for Best Actor in a Supporting Role") for portraying [Jock Delves Broughton](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jock_Delves_Broughton "Jock Delves Broughton") in _[White Mischief](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/White\_Mischief\_(film) "White Mischief (film)")_ (1987).[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Joss_Ackland#cite_note-2)

## Early life

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Joss_Ackland&action=edit&section=1 "Edit section: Early life")]

Sidney Edmond Jocelyn Ackland was born in a basement flat in "then insalubrious" [North Kensington](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/North_Kensington "North Kensington"), London, on [29 February 1928](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Leap_year "Leap year"),[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Joss_Ackland#cite_note-bfi-3) the son of Sydney Norman Ackland (died 1981), an Irish journalist who had been sent to England to live with an aunt by his parents for seducing their maid, but subsequently seduced his aunt's maid, Ruth Izod (died 1957), whom he married.[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Joss_Ackland#cite_note-4)[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Joss_Ackland#cite_note-5)[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Joss_Ackland#cite_note-6) The Acklands' basement flat was one of "a string of similar places" in which they lived, invariably with "one bedroom and the absolute bare essentials"; Ackland described his upbringing in the [Ladbroke Grove](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ladbroke_Grove "Ladbroke Grove") area as being "very poor".[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Joss_Ackland#cite_note-7)[[8]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Joss_Ackland#cite_note-8)

Initially educated at [Dame Alice Owen's School](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dame_Alice_Owen's_School "Dame Alice Owen's School"), Ackland left aged fifteen to become an actor.[[9]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Joss_Ackland#cite_note-9) Thus, Ackland was trained by [Elsie Fogerty](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Elsie_Fogerty "Elsie Fogerty") at the [Central School of Speech and Drama](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Central_School_of_Speech_and_Drama "Central School of Speech and Drama"), then based at the [Royal Albert Hall](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Royal_Albert_Hall "Royal Albert Hall"), London.[[10]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Joss_Ackland#cite_note-10)

Ackland and Rosemary Kirkcaldy were married on 18 August 1951, when Ackland was 23 and she was 22.[[11]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Joss_Ackland#cite_note-scotsman-11) She was an actress and Ackland wooed her when they appeared on stage together in [Pitlochry](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pitlochry "Pitlochry"), Scotland.[[12]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Joss_Ackland#cite_note-12) The couple struggled initially as Ackland's acting career was in its infancy.[[11]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Joss_Ackland#cite_note-scotsman-11) In 1954 they moved to [Lilongwe](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lilongwe "Lilongwe") in what was then [Nyasaland](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nyasaland "Nyasaland"), now Malawi, where Ackland managed a [tea plantation](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tea_plantation "Tea plantation") for six months[[13]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Joss_Ackland#cite_note-TelegraphObitRef-13) but, deciding it was too dangerous, they moved to [Cape Town](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cape_Town "Cape Town"), South Africa.[[11]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Joss_Ackland#cite_note-scotsman-11) Though they both obtained steady acting jobs in South Africa, after two years they returned to England in 1957.[[11]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Joss_Ackland#cite_note-scotsman-11)[[14]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Joss_Ackland#cite_note-bbcnews-14)

## Career

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Joss_Ackland&action=edit&section=2 "Edit section: Career")]

After attending London's Central School of Speech and Drama, he made his professional debut on stage at just 17 years old, starring in the 1945 production of _The Hasty Heart_. Ackland joined the [Old Vic](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Old_Vic "Old Vic"), appearing alongside other notable actors including [Maggie Smith](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Maggie_Smith "Maggie Smith"), [Judi Dench](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Judi_Dench "Judi Dench") and [Tom Courtenay](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tom_Courtenay "Tom Courtenay"). Ackland worked steadily in television and film in the 1960s and 70s.

He worked opposite [Alec Guinness](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Alec_Guinness "Alec Guinness") in the 1979 television serial _[Tinker Tailor Soldier Spy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tinker\_Tailor\_Soldier\_Spy\_(TV\_series) "Tinker Tailor Soldier Spy (TV series)")_, playing sporting journalist and intermittent British espionage operative [Jerry Westerby](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jerry_Westerby "Jerry Westerby"), and his career advanced through the 1980s with important parts in such films as _[The Sicilian](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_Sicilian\_(film) "The Sicilian (film)")_, _[Lethal Weapon 2](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lethal\_Weapon\_2 "Lethal Weapon 2")_, _[The Hunt for Red October](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_Hunt\_for\_Red\_October\_(film) "The Hunt for Red October (film)")_ and _[White Mischief](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/White\_Mischief\_(film) "White Mischief (film)")_.[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Joss_Ackland#cite_note-bfi-3) On television Ackland appeared as Jephro Rucastle with [Jeremy Brett](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jeremy_Brett "Jeremy Brett") and [David Burke](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/David_Burke_(British_actor) "David Burke (British actor)") in _[The Adventures of Sherlock Holmes](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_Adventures\_of\_Sherlock\_Holmes\_(TV\_series) "The Adventures of Sherlock Holmes (TV series)");_ the episode entitled "[The Copper Beeches](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Copper_Beeches "The Copper Beeches")". Other appearances included _[Passion of Mind](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Passion\_of\_Mind "Passion of Mind")_ with [Demi Moore](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Demi_Moore "Demi Moore") and the two-part TV serial _[Hogfather](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Terry\_Pratchett's\_Hogfather "Terry Pratchett's Hogfather")_ based on [Terry Pratchett](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Terry_Pratchett "Terry Pratchett")'s _[Discworld](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Discworld "Discworld")_.[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Joss_Ackland#cite_note-bfi-3) He played [C. S. Lewis](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/C._S._Lewis "C. S. Lewis") in the television version of _[Shadowlands](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shadowlands\_(1985\_film) "Shadowlands (1985 film)")_ before it was adapted into a stage play starring [Nigel Hawthorne](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nigel_Hawthorne "Nigel Hawthorne") and then a theatrical film with [Anthony Hopkins](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Anthony_Hopkins "Anthony Hopkins") in the same role.[[15]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Joss_Ackland#cite_note-15) His voice (as well as that of [Roy Dotrice](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Roy_Dotrice "Roy Dotrice")) was heard reading quotations in several episodes of [Jacob Bronowski](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jacob_Bronowski "Jacob Bronowski")'s 1973 documentary series _[The Ascent of Man](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_Ascent\_of\_Man "The Ascent of Man")_.

His voice was also a mainstay of many British television commercials including [Yellow Pages](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Yellow_Pages "Yellow Pages"), [WK Kellogg Co](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/WK_Kellogg_Co "WK Kellogg Co") and [Homepride](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Homepride "Homepride").[_[citation needed](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wikipedia:Citation\_needed "Wikipedia:Citation needed")_]

Ackland's stage roles included creating the role of [Juan Perón](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Juan_Per%C3%B3n "Juan Perón") in [Tim Rice](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tim_Rice "Tim Rice") and [Andrew Lloyd Webber](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Andrew_Lloyd_Webber "Andrew Lloyd Webber")'s musical _[Evita](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Evita\_(musical) "Evita (musical)")_ opposite [Elaine Paige](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Elaine_Paige "Elaine Paige").[[16]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Joss_Ackland#cite_note-16) He also starred in the London production of [Stephen Sondheim](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Stephen_Sondheim "Stephen Sondheim")'s and [Hugh Wheeler](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hugh_Wheeler "Hugh Wheeler")'s _[A Little Night Music](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/A\_Little\_Night\_Music "A Little Night Music")_ with [Jean Simmons](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jean_Simmons "Jean Simmons") and [Hermione Gingold](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hermione_Gingold "Hermione Gingold"), performing on the RCA Victor original London cast album.[[17]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Joss_Ackland#cite_note-17)

Ackland appeared in the [Pet Shop Boys](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pet_Shop_Boys "Pet Shop Boys")' 1988 film _[It Couldn't Happen Here](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/It\_Couldn't\_Happen\_Here "It Couldn't Happen Here")_, and in the video for their version of the song _[Always on My Mind](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Always\_on\_My\_Mind "Always on My Mind")_, which was taken from the film.[[18]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Joss_Ackland#cite_note-18) Several years later, he said in an interview with the _[Radio Times](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Radio\_Times "Radio Times")_ that he had appeared with the band purely because his grandchildren liked their music.[_[citation needed](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wikipedia:Citation\_needed "Wikipedia:Citation needed")_]

Ackland also co-starred as [Emilio Estevez](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Emilio_Estevez "Emilio Estevez")'s mentor and friend Hans in the 1992 Disney _[The Mighty Ducks](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_Mighty\_Ducks "The Mighty Ducks")_.[[19]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Joss_Ackland#cite_note-19) He reprised the role four years later in 1996's _[D3: The Mighty Ducks](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/D3:\_The\_Mighty\_Ducks "D3: The Mighty Ducks")_.[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Joss_Ackland#cite_note-bfi-3)

In a 2001 interview with the [BBC](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/BBC "BBC"), Ackland said that he had appeared in some "awful" films due to being a [workaholic](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Workaholic "Workaholic"). He said that he "regretted" appearing in _[Bill & Ted's Bogus Journey](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bill\_&\_Ted's\_Bogus\_Journey "Bill & Ted's Bogus Journey")_ and the Pet Shop Boys music video. He also criticised former co-star Demi Moore as "not very bright or talented",[[14]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Joss_Ackland#cite_note-bbcnews-14) though he worked with her again years later in _[Flawless](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Flawless\_(2008\_film) "Flawless (2008 film)")_ (2008).

Also in 2007, Ackland appeared in the film _[How About You](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/How\_About\_You\_(film) "How About You (film)")_ opposite [Vanessa Redgrave](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Vanessa_Redgrave "Vanessa Redgrave"), portraying a recovering alcoholic living in a residential home after being forced to retire and losing his wife to cancer.[[20]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Joss_Ackland#cite_note-20)

In 2008, Ackland returned to the small screen as Sir Freddy Butler, a much married baronet, in the [ITV1](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/ITV1 "ITV1") show _[Midsomer Murders](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Midsomer\_Murders "Midsomer Murders")_. The episode was entitled _Vixens Run_.[[21]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Joss_Ackland#cite_note-21)

In September 2013, [Jonathan Miller](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jonathan_Miller "Jonathan Miller") directed a Gala Performance of [William Shakespeare](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/William_Shakespeare "William Shakespeare")'s _[King Lear](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/King\_Lear "King Lear")_ at the Old Vic in London, with Ackland in the role of Lear.[[22]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Joss_Ackland#cite_note-22)

## Personal life and death

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Joss_Ackland&action=edit&section=3 "Edit section: Personal life and death")]

Ackland and his wife Rosemary (née Kirkcaldy) were married for 51 years. They had seven children,[[23]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Joss_Ackland#cite_note-23) thirty-two grandchildren and eight great-grandchildren.[[24]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Joss_Ackland#cite_note-24) Despite his filming taking him to far-flung locations, he said Rosemary and he "were hardly ever apart".[[25]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Joss_Ackland#cite_note-25) Daughter Kirsty married Anthony Shawn [Baring](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Baring_family "Baring family"), a descendant of the merchant banker [Sir Francis Baring, 1st Baronet](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sir_Francis_Baring,_1st_Baronet "Sir Francis Baring, 1st Baronet") and a descendant of [Robert Rundell](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Robert_Rundell_Guinness "Robert Rundell Guinness")[Guinness](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Guinness_family "Guinness family"), founder of the merchant bank [Guinness Mahon](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Guinness_Mahon "Guinness Mahon").[[26]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Joss_Ackland#cite_note-26)[[27]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Joss_Ackland#cite_note-27)

In 1963, their house in [Barnes](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Barnes,_London "Barnes, London") caught fire. Rosemary, who was pregnant at the time, saved their five children but broke her back when jumping from the bedroom window.[[28]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Joss_Ackland#cite_note-28) She was told she would miscarry and never walk again, but she later gave birth and after 18 months in [Stoke Mandeville Hospital](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Stoke_Mandeville_Hospital "Stoke Mandeville Hospital"), was able to walk again.[[29]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Joss_Ackland#cite_note-29)[[11]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Joss_Ackland#cite_note-scotsman-11) Their eldest son, Paul, died of a [heroin overdose](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Heroin_overdose "Heroin overdose") in 1982, aged 29.[[30]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Joss_Ackland#cite_note-30) In 2000, Rosemary was diagnosed with [motor neurone disease](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Motor_neurone_disease "Motor neurone disease"); she died on 25 July 2002.[[13]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Joss_Ackland#cite_note-TelegraphObitRef-13)

In 2020, Ackland participated in the "Letters Live" project, and was recorded from his home in [Clovelly](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Clovelly "Clovelly"), Devon.[[31]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Joss_Ackland#cite_note-31) His letter reflected on the [COVID-19 crisis](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/COVID-19_pandemic_in_the_United_Kingdom "COVID-19 pandemic in the United Kingdom") and his hopes for how the country could draw "strength from adversity".[[32]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Joss_Ackland#cite_note-32)

Ackland died at home in Clovelly, on 19 November 2023, aged 95.[[33]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Joss_Ackland#cite_note-33)[[34]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Joss_Ackland#cite_note-34)
